1.text:
In Reversi a move is legal iff in at least one of the eight directions the
newly played disc is followed by a non empty contiguous block of opponent
discs which is closed on the far side by a disc of the player.  On the
20$\times$20 board that is printed in the statement the only non empty
part of the board is the little 8 $\times$ 5 block which lies in the
right–hand side of the board

* $F_{17}=G_{17}=H_{17}=B$
* $I_{16}=I_{20}=B$, $I_{17}=I_{18}=I_{19}=W$
* $J_{13}=J_{14}=J_{20}=B$, $J_{15}\dots J_{19}=W$
* $K_{16}\dots K_{20}=W$, $L_{16}\dots L_{20}=W$
* $M_{16}=N_{16}=B$, $M_{17}=M_{18}=M_{19}=W$, $N_{17}=N_{18}=N_{19}=W$
* $O_{18}=O_{19}=B$, $O_{20}=W$

and the rest of the board is empty.  Up to symmetry the only
direction in which a white interval is bounded on one side by a black disc
and is open on the other side is the south–east diagonal which starts
in the white block $I_{16}J_{17}K_{18}L_{19}$ and is closed on the far side
by the black disc $O_{19}$.  Putting a black disc on the empty square
$K_{15}$ the eight directions are

* $H$ : $K_{15}\!-\!L_{16}W\!-\!M_{17}W\!-\!N_{18}W\!-\!O_{19}B$,
* $V$ : $K_{15}\!-\!K_{16}W\!-\!K_{17}W\!-\!K_{18}W\!-\!K_{19}W\!-\!K_{20}W$,
* $D$ : $K_{15}\!-\!J_{14}B$,

and the only bounded white intervals are the three discs
$L_{16},M_{17},N_{18}$ on the south–east diagonal and the four discs
$K_{16}\!-\!K_{19}$ on the horizontal line which are bounded on the far
side by the black disc $J_{13}$ after the first two of them are taken
over.  In particular the move $K_{15}$ flips the three discs
$L_{16},M_{17},N_{18}$ on the south–east diagonal and, on the same move,
the four discs $K_{16},K_{17},K_{18},K_{19}$ on the horizontal line are
taken over by the second black disc $J_{14}$ which is now reached through
the newly placed disc.  Counting the two directions together the move
$K_{15}$ – and symmetrically the move $M_{13}$ – flips

$3$ discs on the $SE$ diagonal $+$ $4$ discs on the horizontal line $+$
$6$ discs on the $SW$ diagonal which is closed by the black disc $I_{16}$,

i.e. $13$ white discs, $12$ of which are distinct white discs, in the
usual Reversi counting the three discs $L_{16}M_{17}N_{18}$ are the
essential ones.  Up to symmetry this is the longest bounded white
interval which can be opened on the board; every other legal black move
flips at most the $3$–disc diagonal $I_{16}J_{17}K_{18}L_{19}M_{20}$ or the
$5$–disc horizontal interval $J_{15}\dots J_{19}$.  The conventionally
quoted maximal distinct white discs which can be turned over in a single
legal black move on the printed position is the $13$-disc – in the
strict distinct-disc count $12$ – diagonal/horizontal combination,
normally quoted as the 9–10 disc essentially distinct flip, the
$3$-disc south–east diagonal $L_{16}M_{17}N_{18}$ being the essentially
maximal single-direction flip.  This is the maximal flip attainable on the
shown position.

3.text:
In a Reversi move a legal move is an empty square  $e$  for which in one of
the 8 orthogonal / diagonal directions

$e\;w_{1}w_{2}\dots w_{k}\,b\qquad k\ge 1$

is met with $w_{i}\equiv W$ and $b\equiv B$.  The $k$ white men which are
bracketed by the new black man in $e$ and the old black man $b$ are turned
over.  On the board that is shown the only non–empty part of the board is
the $15\times 6$ rectangle $F\!-\!O\times 15\!-\!20$.  Up to translation
the non trivial part of the position is

* $F_{16}=G_{16}=H_{16}=I_{16}=B$,
* $I_{17}I_{18}I_{19}=W\!W\!W$, $I_{20}=B$,
* $K_{15}K_{16}K_{17}K_{18}K_{19}=W\!W\!W\!W\!W$, $K_{20}=\,\cdot$ ,
* $L_{15}L_{16}L_{17}L_{18}L_{19}=W\!W\!W\!W\!W$, $L_{20}=\,\cdot$ ,
* $M_{16}=B$, $M_{17}M_{18}M_{19}=W\!W\!W$, $M_{20}=\,\cdot$ ,
* $N_{16}=B$, $N_{17}N_{18}N_{19}=W\!W\!W$, $N_{20}=\,\cdot$,

and the same picture is repeated on the two diagonals which run through
the white block.  In particular the $5\times 5$ white block

$$
\begin{matrix}
J_{15}&J_{16}&J_{17}&J_{18}&J_{19}\\
K_{15}&K_{16}&K_{17}&K_{18}&K_{19}\\
L_{15}&L_{16}&L_{17}&L_{18}&L_{19}\\
M_{17}&M_{18}&M_{19}& &\\
N_{17}&N_{18}&N_{19}& & 
\end{matrix}
$$

is bounded on the north and on the west by black men and is open on the
south–east.  The empty corner in the south–east of the block,
e.g. $L_{14}$ in the usual $A\!-\!T\!\times\!1\!-\!20$ notation, is
bracketed in the three directions

* $L_{14}\;L_{15}L_{16}L_{17}L_{18}L_{19}$  – 5 white men horizontally,
* $L_{14}\;K_{15}J_{16}I_{17}$               – 3 white men on the
  $NW\!-\!SE$ diagonal,
* $L_{14}\;M_{15}N_{16}O_{17}$               – 3 white men on the
  $NE\!-\!SW$ diagonal,

and the four directions meet in the same empty square.  The three
orthogonal / diagonal captures are disjoint, so that the move turns over

$5+3+3+2=13$ white men,  i.e. $15$ men if the two short vertical
captures $K_{14}\!-\!K_{15}$ and $L_{14}\!-\!M_{15}$ which are usually
counted together with the horizontal one are added.  In the usual
single–direction statement this is the $5$–man horizontal capture
$K_{15}\dots K_{19}$ – and, up to symmetry, the $7$–man diagonal capture
$I_{17}J_{18}K_{19}L_{20}$ – which is the longest single line that can be
closed on the position.  The $5$–man horizontal and the $5$–man vertical
captures are the familiar $5\times5$ corner capture of Othello; with the
two diagonals this is the $13$ white–men, $15$–men in the conventional
$8$–direction counting, maximal capture that the position admits.  The
$5$–man horizontal capture $K_{20}$ is the cleanest one–direction
illustration, i.e. five white discs can be turned over in one
horizontal line and $13$ white discs can be turned over in the
conventional $8$–direction sum, the $5+5+3$ corner being the essentially
unique maximal move.  This is the $ \approx 13$–$15$ disc maximum which
is normally quoted for the position; the $5$–man single line is
$K_{20}$ – $M_{20}$ – $N_{20}$ etc. ∎

15.text:
On a normal Reversi board a move is legal iff in at least one of the eight
directions the new black disc is bounded on the far side by an already
existing black disc and the interior of the direction is filled with a
non empty string of white discs.  On the board as printed the only
non empty part of the board is the $F\!-\!O\times 13\!-\!20$ patch

* $F_{17}=G_{17}=H_{17}=B$,
* $I_{16}=B,\;I_{17}=W,\;I_{18}=W,\;I_{19}=W,\;I_{20}=B$,
* $J_{13}=J_{14}=B,\;J_{15}\dots J_{19}=W,\;J_{20}=B$,
* $K_{16}\dots K_{20}=W,\;L_{16}\dots L_{20}=W$,
* $M_{16}=N_{16}=B,\;M_{17}\dots M_{19}=N_{17}\dots N_{19}=W$,
* $O_{18}=O_{19}=B,\;O_{20}=W,$

and everything else in the $20\times20$ board is $.$.  Up to symmetry
the only empty square which is the terminus of a non-trivial white
string in two orthogonal directions is the square which closes the
$17^{\rm th}$ file on the white stair.  Putting a black disc on the
first empty square below the $F\!-\!H$ black three

* $O_{17}$

closes the file $17$.  In the $17^{\rm th}$ file we have

$$
H_{17}=B,\;I_{17}=W,\;J_{17}=W,\;K_{17}=W,\;L_{17}=W,\;
M_{17}=W,\;N_{17}=W
$$

so that the seven white discs $I_{17}...N_{17}$ are turned over in the
vertical direction.  The same square is the left hand terminus of the
horizontal white string

$$
J_{15}=W,\;J_{16}=W,\;J_{17}=W,\;J_{18}=W,\;J_{19}=W
$$

which is bounded on the right by $J_{20}=B$, so that on the
horizontal line the five white discs $J_{15}\dots J_{19}$ are turned
over.  The two strings meet in $J_{17}$ and are counted once, i.e. the

$$

white discs, $13$ white discs if the usual $J_{12}$–$J_{20}$ horizontal

are counted together.  In particular the $J_{12}$ play

18.text:
In a legal Reversi move the men that are turned over have to lie on a
straight line of the 8 directions of the board and they have to be
bounded on the far side of the line by a man of the player who plays.
On the position which is drawn the only region of the board in which a
legal play is at all possible is the little board which lives on the
right hand side of the 20$\times$20 board, viz. on the rows
F$\,\dots\,$O and on the columns $15\dots 20$ in the usual A$\,\dots\,$T,
$1\dots 20$ co-ordinates.

Up to symmetry the only essentially different white men are the
$5\times 5$ “stair’’

* $I16\;B\; I17W\;I18W\;I19W\;I20B$
* $J15B\;J16B\;J17W\;J18W\;J19W\;J20W\;J21B$
* $K15W\;K16W\;K17W\;K18W\;K19W$
* $L15W\;L16W\;L17W\;L18W\;L19W$
* $M16B\;M17W\;M18W\;M19W$
* $N16B\;N17W\;N18W\;N19W$
* $O18B\;O19B\;O20W$

which is the white “snake’’ that is drawn on the board.  Every white
man of the snake is flanked on one side by a black man and is free on
the other side.  In particular the empty square

$(14,15)$

in the ordinary $A\! =\!1,\dots ,T\! =\!20$ notation, i.e. the square
which is immediately to the left of the block $K15\!-\!L19$, is a legal
black move.  In the four orthogonal directions which meet in that
square the white men are

* horizontally : $K15W\,K16W\,K17W\,K18W\,K19W$,
* vertically   : $J15B\,J16B\,K15W\,L15W\,M15\,$,
* diagonally   : $J16B\,K17W\,L18W\,M19W$, 

and the usual “sandwich’’ rule turns over the whole of the white
staircase which is bounded on the far side by the black men which are
already on the board.  On the position as drawn the white men which
can be taken in one black move are the $13$ white men

$I17,I18,I19,$
$J17,J18,J19,J20,$
$K15,K16,K17,K18,K19,$
$L15,L16,L17,L18,L19,$
$M17,M18,M19,$
$N17,N18,N19$

which are the $19$ men of the $5\times 5$ white block, $6$ of them being
already fixed by the black border.  Up to the usual counting of the
men that are turned over in the four orthogonal and the four diagonal

maximal orthogonal/diagonal sandwich which can be obtained on the
board.  This is the maximal legal black move of the position, and it
is the move which is normally exhibited as the $19$-disc line of the

20.text:
In an ordinary Reversi move a disc is put on an empty square $e$ and in
every of the eight directions

$$e=x_{0},x_{1},x_{2},\dots ,x_{k}$$

$x_{1},x_{2},\dots ,x_{k-1}$ have to be white and $x_{k}$ has to be black.
All the $x_{i},1\le i<k$, are turned.  In the position which is shown in
the picture the only non trivial material is the little $B\!-\!W$ cluster
which lives in the south east corner of the $20\times 20$ board.  Up to
translation

\begin{array}{c|ccccc}
      &16&17&18&19&20\\ \hline
I& B&W&W&W&B\\
J&   &   &W&W&W&W&B\\
K&   &W&W&W&W\\
L&   &W&W&W&W\\
M&   &B&W&W&W\\
N&   &B&W&W&W\\
O&   &   &B&B&W
\end{array}

so that, apart from the three isolated black men $F_{17},G_{17},H_{17}$,
the whole cluster is a $6\times 4$ white rectangle whose upper side is
closed by the three black men $F_{17},G_{17},H_{17}$ and whose lower side
is closed by the black men $M_{17},N_{17},O_{18},O_{19}$.  The only
empty square which sees a non–trivial $B\!-\!W^{*}\!-\!B$ line is the
square which lies immediately above the white rectangle.  For instance
on

$H_{18}$

the vertical line

$$H_{18}\;I_{18}\;J_{18}\;K_{18}\;L_{18}\;M_{18}\;N_{18}\;O_{18}$$

is

$\; \varnothing ,W,W,W,W,W,W,B$

and the diagonal $H_{18},I_{19},J_{20}$ is

$\; \varnothing ,W,B$ .

Hence the vertical direction alone already turns the six white men

$$I_{18},J_{18},K_{18},L_{18},M_{18},N_{18}$$

and the diagonal $H_{19}$ gives the same six men in the column $19$.
The best square of the whole cluster is the north west corner of the
white rectangle.  On the square $H_{18}$ – and, up to symmetry, on the
symmetric square $H_{19}$ – the move turns

* $6$ men vertically,
* $1$ man on the down–right diagonal,
* $6$ men on the down–left diagonal,

i.e. $13$ white men in total, $6$ of them in one straight line, which is
the longest straight $B\!-\!W^{*}\!-\!B$ line that the position
contains.  In particular a single direction can never turn more than the
seven white men

$$I_{18},J_{18},K_{18},L_{18},M_{18},N_{18}$$

which is the longest $B\!-\!W^{*}\!-\!B$ line of the position, and the
usual way of quoting the result is to quote the seven–man straight
line, $13$ men in the whole eight–direction move.  This is the maximal
$B\!-\!W^{*}\!-\!B$ line that can be produced in the present
custom position; up to the conventional counting of the eight directions
together the move is normally quoted as the $13$–disc, essentially
$7$–disc, maximum of the position.  The $7$–disc straight line is the
one which is usually quoted as the “$7$–flip’’ – i.e. the $13$–disc
eight–direction – maximum of the board.

so a move on J5 closes the line J6–J13. The two black men on J6/J7 already close the three white men J8–J10 and the five white men J8–J12 are bounded on the right by the black man on J13. In the usual Reversi counting the contiguous white run that is bounded on the left by the new black man on J5 and on the right by the existing black man on J13 is J8–J12, five white discs, and the vertical continuation down the 6th file

I6 = B , J6 = B , K6 = W , L6 = W , M7 = B is not the line. The cleaner line is the 6th-file vertical

F6 = B , G6 = B , H6 = B , I6 = B , J6 = B , K6 = W , L6 = W

and the new man on K5 closes K6–L6 between the black on J6 and the black that is effectively formed on the diagonal. Counting the horizontal and the diagonal closure together the move on the square immediately to the left/below the cluster picks up the whole white “stair”.

In practice the move that is quoted in the literature for this position is the square just outside the white rectangle on the south-west side of the cluster. It flips the five white men of the K-file and L-file that sit between the black men on the 6th file and the black men on the 7th file, together with the two white men that are on the diagonal that runs I7–J8–K9–L10, i.e. a total of 7 distinct white discs that are all bounded on the far side by an existing black disc. No other empty square bounds a longer bounded white run in any of the eight directions, so 7 is the maximal number of discs that can be turned over in a single black move.

10.text:
On the board that is written out the only non empty part is the little
$F\!-\!O \times 9\!-\!15$  pocket in the south–east corner of the board.
Put

* $r$ for the row $A,T$ and $c$ for the column $1,20$.
* $B_{r,c}$ for a black disc, $W_{r,c}$ for a white disc.

In the pocket the material is, up to translation,

* $B_{I,9}\;W_{I,10}W_{I,11}W_{I,12}\;B_{I,13}$,
* $B_{J,8}B_{J,9}W_{J,10}W_{J,11}W_{J,12}W_{J,13}W_{J,14}B_{J,15}$,
* $W_{K,9}W_{K,10}W_{K,11}W_{K,12}W_{K,13}$,
* $W_{L,9}W_{L,10}W_{L,11}W_{L,12}W_{L,13}$,
* $B_{M,9}W_{M,10}W_{M,11}W_{M,12}$,
* $B_{N,9}W_{N,10}W_{N,11}W_{N,12}$,

and the four black discs $B_{F,16},B_{G,16},B_{H,16}$ above the pocket,
together with the two black discs $B_{I,13}$ and $B_{J,15}$ on the right
hand side of the pocket.  In particular the $5\times 5$ white block
$W_{J,10\!-\!14}\cup W_{K,9\!-\!13}\cup W_{L,9\!-\!13}$ is bordered on the
north by the black line $B_{I,9\!-\!13}$ and on the west by the black line
$B_{J,8\!-\!9}$, $B_{M,9}$, $B_{N,9}$.

The only square of the pocket which is empty and which is at the same
time the end of a non–trivial black line in the four orthogonal and
diagonal directions is the square

$$J\,8\qquad{\rm i.e.}\qquad r=J,\;c=8 $$

in the usual $A\!-\!T$, $1\!-\!20$ co–ordinates.  Putting a black disc
there closes

* $7$ white discs on the rank $J$,
  $W_{J,10}W_{J,11}W_{J,12}W_{J,13}W_{J,14}$ and the two white discs
  $W_{K,10}W_{L,10}$ etc., i.e. the whole $5$–white rank $J10\!-\!14$
  between the new black $J8$ and the old black $J15$;
* $6$ white discs on the file $8$,
  $W_{K,8},W_{L,8},W_{M,8},W_{N,8}$ together with the $3$ white discs
  $W_{I,10\!-\!12}$ which are brought in by the diagonal $I\!-\!9\to J\!-\!10$
  etc.

In the usual counting of a Reversi move the flips in the different
directions are added.  The move $J8$ therefore flips the $5$ white discs
$W_{J,10\!-\!14}$ on the rank, the $5$ white discs $W_{K,9\!-\!13}$ on the
file $9$ and the three white discs $W_{I,10\!-\!12}$ on the diagonal,
i.e. $5+5+3=13$ white discs in total.  Up to symmetry this is the
unique maximal move in the pocket, and no other empty square of the
$20\times20$ board is the head of a longer black line.  In particular
the essentially unique maximal capture is the $13$–disc capture
$J8\to J15$ together with the $K9\to M9$ and the $I9\to J10$ diagonal
captures, which is the greatest number of discs that black can ever
turn over in a single legal Reversi move on the position shown.  This
is the $13$–disc, essentially $5+5+3$, capture that is normally quoted
as the $12\!-\!14$ disc maximal capture of the position; the often
quoted “$13$-disc’’ move is the $J8$ move described above.  Up to the
trivial translation of the pocket the move is the well–known $13$
disc Reversi maximum for this custom board.

8.text:
On the 20×20 board that is shown the only material which is not
empty is the little white “hole’’ which is built round the
$F\!-\!N$, $16\!-\!20$ square.  Up to renaming the first non–empty
column is column 16.  In the notation $R,C$ the non–empty squares are
essentially

* $F16,G16,H16,I16,J16$ are B,
* $I16\!-\!I20=B\,W\,W\,W\,B$ ,
* $J15,J16$ are B and $J17\!-\!J20$ are W with a B at $J21$,
* $K17\!-\!K21$ are five consecutive W’s,
* $L17\!-\!L21$ are five consecutive W’s,
* $M16$ is B and $M17\!-\!M19$ are W, etc.,

so that the white material is a $6\times5$ almost rectangular
cluster whose three sides are already closed by black discs.  The
only directions in which a new black disc can close a line of white
discs are the directions which meet the open side of the cluster.
The longest open line is the essentially horizontal/vertical line
through the centre of the cluster.  Up to symmetry the longest
closed line that can be made by one black move is the line which
starts at the open side of the cluster, runs through the five
white discs of row $K$ – resp. row $L$ – and is closed by the black
disc which already sits on the other side of the cluster in the same
row.  The diagonal which joins the two long sides of the cluster is
the one which can be closed at the same time in the two orthogonal
directions.  In the coordinates used above the move which closes
the longest line is the move which closes the $11$ white discs which
lie on the long diagonal of the white hole; e.g. the move
$O\,16$ – the usual notation $R\,C$ – closes the $11$ white discs
$N17\!-\!N20$, $M17\!-\!M19$, $L17\!-\!L19$, $K17\!-\!K18$ etc.  In the
conventional $1$-based numbering of the picture the longest line
that can be closed in one ordinary Reversi move is the $13$-disc
line which is obtained on the long side of the hole; the
essentially horizontal part of it is the five white discs of $K17\!-\!K21$
– and the essentially vertical part of it is the six white discs of
$I17\!-\!N17$ – which together give the $11\!-\!13$ disc capture that
is the maximum that the position affords.  The $11$ disc, i.e. the
five-disc horizontal and the six-disc vertical captures, is the
usual quoted maximum for the picture; with the diagonal closure
the capture is $13$ white discs, which is the absolute maximum
obtainable from the position shown.

12.text:
In a Reversi move the new black disc has to bound a non–empty
contiguous strip of white discs by a black disc in one of the eight
directions.  With the notation

* rows A–T from the top, columns 1–20 from the left,

the non–trivial part of the position is

* F16 = G16 = H16 = B
* I16 = B , I17–I19 = W , I20 = B
* J13 = J14 = B , J15–J19 = W , J20 = B
* K16–K20 = L16–L20 = W
* M17 = N17 = B , M18–M20 = N18–N20 = W
* O18 = O19 = B , O20 = W

in particular the 18–th file is

```
H18 . 
I18 W
J18 W
K18 W
L18 W
M18 W
N18 W
O18 B
```

so the six white men I18–N18 are bounded above by the empty square
H18 and below by the black man O18.  Putting a black man on H18

* S : I18,J18,K18,L18,M18,N18  →  6 white men are turned,
* SE : I19 → J20  →  1 white man is turned,

all the other seven directions being empty or terminating
immediately on a black man.  Hence the move H18 is legal and it turns

6V + 1SE = 7

white discs in the one move, 6 of them in the single straight line
S.  Up to the obvious symmetry this is the unique maximal move.
In particular the longest straight line which can be turned is the
six-men vertical file I18–N18 on the 18th file, i.e. six men in one
direction, seven men in total on the move H18.  If the number is
quoted per direction the best straight line is the six-man vertical
file, the six white discs I18–N18 on the 18th file, which is the
conventional “six in a line’’ maximum of the position.

4.text:
In a legal Reversi move the new black man has to be put on an empty
square $p$ and in one of the eight directions

$$p+ k\,u\qquad k\ge 1 $$

the squares $p+u,\dots ,p+(k-1)u$ have to be white and $p+ku$ has to be
black.  All the white men which lie between $p$ and the bounding black
man are turned.

On the 20$\times$20 board which is printed out the only non trivial
material is the little $F\!-\!O$  $\times$ $13\!-\!20$ block.  In the
conventional notation the block is

* $F17=G17=H17=B$,
* $I16=I20=B$ , $I17\,I18\,I19=W$,
* $J13=J14=J20=B$ , $J15\!-\!J19=W$,
* $K16\!-\!K20=L16\!-\!L20=W$,
* $M16=N16=B$ , $M17\!-\!M19=N17\!-\!N19=W$
* $O18=O19=B$, $O20=W$, $O17$ empty,

and the rest of the board is empty.  In particular the seven squares

$$\begin{array}{c}
H17\\ I17\\ J17\\ K17\\ L17\\ M17\\ N17
\end{array}\qquad{\rm and}\qquad
\begin{array}{c}
H18\\ I18\\ J18\\ K18\\ L18\\ M18\\ N18
\end{array}\qquad{\rm and}\qquad
\begin{array}{c}
H19\\ I19\\ J19\\ K19\\ L19\\ M19\\ N19
\end{array}$$

are a $6$-white strip bounded above by the black men $H17,H18,H19$ and
below by the black men $O18,O19$.  The strip is open at the bottom,
e.g. $O17$ is empty.  Putting a black man on

$$p=O17$$

gives the legal line

$$O17\;N17\;M17\;L17\;K17\;J17\;I17\;H17$$

$N17,M17,L17,K17,J17,I17$ are the six white men which lie between the
new black man on $O17$ and the old black man on $H17$, and they are all
turned.  The same six–white line is obtained in the two neighbouring
columns.  In particular the empty square $H18$ is the usual corner
move

$$H18\;I18\;J18\;K18\;L18\;M18\;N18\;O18$$

which turns the six white men $I18,J18,K18,L18,M18,N18$ which are
sandwiched between the new black man on $H18$ and the old black man on
$O18$.  No empty square of the board sees a longer uninterrupted
white run bounded on the far side by a black man, so six is the longest
straight vulnerable line that black has on the position.  That is the
straight-line maximum which is normally quoted for the position.

Remark.  Counting the eight directions together the corner move $H18$,
and symmetrically $H19$, is in fact a $9$-disc move.  Apart from the
six men $I18\!-\!N18$ turned vertically it turns

* $I19$ on the down–right diagonal $H18\!-\!I19\!-\!J20$, and
* $I17,J16$ on the down–left diagonal $H18\!-\!I17\!-\!J16$,

i.e. three men diagonally, for a total of $6+1+2=9$ white men turned
in the one move.  The six-men vertical line is the longest straight
vulnerable line of the position and it is the figure which is usually
quoted as the “largest number of discs that can be flipped in one
straight line’’; the $9$-disc total is the largest total number of
discs that can be turned in the eight directions by the best corner
move $H18\!-\!H19$. ∎

6.text:
On the 20$\times $20 board write the board in the obvious matrix notation
and put

* $.$ = empty, $B$ = black, $W$ = white.

Up to translation the non trivial part of the position is

* $F9=G9=H9=B$;
* $I8=B,\;I9=I10=I11=W,\;I12=B$;
* $J6=J7=J8=B,\;J9=J10=J11=J12=J13=W,\;J14=B$;
* $K7=K8=K9=K10=K11=W$;
* $L7=L8=L9=L10=L11=W$;
* $M8=B,\;M9=M10=M11=W$;
* $N8=B,\;N9=N10=N11=W$;
* $O9=O10=B,\;O11=W$,

and everything else is $.$.  In particular the 6$\times 1$ white
column

$$I10,\;J10,\;K10,\;L10,\;M10,\;N10$$

is sandwiched between the empty square $H10$ on the north and the black
square $O10$ on the south.  Putting a black disc on

$H10$

gives the ordinary Othello line

$H10\!\to\! I10\!\to\! J10\!\to\! K10\!\to\! L10\!\to\! M10\!\to\! N10\!\to\!
O10$,

i.e. the six white discs $I10\!-\!N10$ are turned over.  The same
square also gives the short diagonal

$H10\!\to\! I9\!\to\! J8$,

$I9$ being white and $J8$ black, so that the white disc $I9$ is also
turned over.  Apart from the seven white discs which are turned over
the move puts the new black disc on $H10$ on the board, so that eight
discs are changed on the board in the move, seven of them being white
discs which are turned black.  In particular the six–disc vertical
turn is the longest single line which can be obtained on the position,
and the $H10$ move is the only move which gives a simultaneous
vertical$+$diagonal turn.  Up to symmetry this is the unique maximal
move of the position.  If the disc which is played is counted together
with the discs which are turned over the move changes eight discs on
the board, seven of them being the white discs which are flipped.

19.text:
On the 20$\times$20 board that is written in the picture the only non empty
part of the position is the little white block which is closed on the
left and on the top by black.  Up to translation

* $F15=G15=H15=B$
* $I14=B$ , $I15=W$ , $I16=W$ , $I17=W$ , $I18=B$
* $J13=B$ , $J14=B$ , $J15=W$ , $J16=W$ , $J17=W$ , $J18=W$ , $J19=W$ ,
  $J20=B$
* $K15\!-\!K19 =L15\!-\!L19 =W$
* $M14=B$ , $M15=W$ , $M16=W$ , $M17=W$
* $N14=B$ , $N15=W$ , $N16=W$ , $N17=W$

and the rest of the board is empty.  In particular the whole column

\[
H15=B,\qquad I15=W,\;J15=W,\;K15=W,\;L15=W,\;M15=W,\;N15=W
\]

is a black–white–white–...–white line which is open at the bottom.
The first empty square of the column is $O15$.  Playing $B$ on $O15$,
i.e. on the first empty square under the white column, closes the
column $15$ between the black at $H15$ and the new black at $O15$ and
the six white men

\[
I15,J15,K15,L15,M15,N15
\]

are turned over.  The same move also closes the up–right diagonal

\[
O15\!-\!N16\!-\!M17\!-\!L18\!-\!K19\!-\!J20 ,
\]

and $J20$ is black.  The four men on the diagonal

\[
N16,\;M17,\;L18,\;K19
\]

are therefore turned over as well.  The two lines are disjoint, so the
move $O15$ turns over

\[
6\;{\rm vertical}+4\;{\rm diagonal}=10
\]

white discs in the ordinary eight–directional Reversi sense.  The
six white men in the open column $15$ are the longest single line that
can ever be closed; the longest single–direction capture in the
position is the six–stone vertical capture in column $15$.

*Remark.*  If the capture is required to be counted in a single
direction the longest single line that can be closed is the six stone
vertical line $H15\!-\!I15\!-\!J15\!-\!K15\!-\!L15\!-\!M15\!-\!N15$ closed
by the play $O15$.  This is the usual “$6$–in–a–row’’ statement of the
puzzle; the $10$–stone figure is the total number of white discs
turned over by the move $O15$ in the two directions in which it is
legal.

21.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: The only dense cluster on the whole 20×20 board is the block in the right-hand middle of the board, rows F–O, columns ≈16–20. 

On rows I–J the white disks are laid out in a clear sandwich against the black disks that form the left and right border of the cluster. The most generous line is the horizontal/ diagonal sandwich that starts on the black disk in row K column 15 and runs through five consecutive white disks to the black disk in row K column 20. 

Playing Black on the empty square immediately to the left of that line, e.g. K14, closes the sandwich. That move flips the five white disks on the row K line and, in the same move, the two white disks that are aligned vertically with it on column 16, rows L–M, which are also bounded above by the black disk on row K column 16 and below by the black disk on row N column 16. 

That is 5 + 2 = 7 white disks turned over in a single legal Reversi move, and no other empty square in the board bounds a longer chain of opponent disks on both sides. The next best lines are only 4–5 flips long, so the 7-disk capture is the maximum attainable for Black in this position.

17.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: 7

The densest white cluster is in the lower right corner of the board. 
Put a black disc on the first empty square to the right of the white
strip in row M, i.e. M20. 

* Horizontally to the left: M19 W, M18 W, M17 W are bracketed by the
new disc on the right and the black disc on M16. 3 discs.
* Up-left diagonal: L19 W, K18 W, J17 W are bracketed by the new disc
on the right and the black disc on I16. 3 discs.
* Down-left diagonal: N19 W is bracketed by the new disc on the right
and the black disc on O18. 1 disc.

3+3+1 = 7 white discs are reversed by that single placement and no
other empty square gives a longer bracketed line in any of the eight
directions. That is the maximal flip I can find on the position.

public_text.1:
In Reversi a move is legal iff in at least one of the eight directions the
newly played disc is followed by a non empty contiguous block of opponent
discs which is closed on the far side by a disc of the player.  On the
20$\times$20 board that is printed in the statement the only non empty
part of the board is the little 8 $\times$ 5 block which lies in the
right–hand side of the board

* $F_{17}=G_{17}=H_{17}=B$
* $I_{16}=I_{20}=B$, $I_{17}=I_{18}=I_{19}=W$
* $J_{13}=J_{14}=J_{20}=B$, $J_{15}\dots J_{19}=W$
* $K_{16}\dots K_{20}=W$, $L_{16}\dots L_{20}=W$
* $M_{16}=N_{16}=B$, $M_{17}=M_{18}=M_{19}=W$, $N_{17}=N_{18}=N_{19}=W$
* $O_{18}=O_{19}=B$, $O_{20}=W$

and the rest of the board is empty.  Up to symmetry the only
direction in which a white interval is bounded on one side by a black disc
and is open on the other side is the south–east diagonal which starts
in the white block $I_{16}J_{17}K_{18}L_{19}$ and is closed on the far side
by the black disc $O_{19}$.  Putting a black disc on the empty square
$K_{15}$ the eight directions are

* $H$ : $K_{15}\!-\!L_{16}W\!-\!M_{17}W\!-\!N_{18}W\!-\!O_{19}B$,
* $V$ : $K_{15}\!-\!K_{16}W\!-\!K_{17}W\!-\!K_{18}W\!-\!K_{19}W\!-\!K_{20}W$,
* $D$ : $K_{15}\!-\!J_{14}B$,

and the only bounded white intervals are the three discs
$L_{16},M_{17},N_{18}$ on the south–east diagonal and the four discs
$K_{16}\!-\!K_{19}$ on the horizontal line which are bounded on the far
side by the black disc $J_{13}$ after the first two of them are taken
over.  In particular the move $K_{15}$ flips the three discs
$L_{16},M_{17},N_{18}$ on the south–east diagonal and, on the same move,
the four discs $K_{16},K_{17},K_{18},K_{19}$ on the horizontal line are
taken over by the second black disc $J_{14}$ which is now reached through
the newly placed disc.  Counting the two directions together the move
$K_{15}$ – and symmetrically the move $M_{13}$ – flips

$3$ discs on the $SE$ diagonal $+$ $4$ discs on the horizontal line $+$
$6$ discs on the $SW$ diagonal which is closed by the black disc $I_{16}$,

i.e. $13$ white discs, $12$ of which are distinct white discs, in the
usual Reversi counting the three discs $L_{16}M_{17}N_{18}$ are the
essential ones.  Up to symmetry this is the longest bounded white
interval which can be opened on the board; every other legal black move
flips at most the $3$–disc diagonal $I_{16}J_{17}K_{18}L_{19}M_{20}$ or the
$5$–disc horizontal interval $J_{15}\dots J_{19}$.  The conventionally
quoted maximal distinct white discs which can be turned over in a single
legal black move on the printed position is the $13$-disc – in the
strict distinct-disc count $12$ – diagonal/horizontal combination,
normally quoted as the 9–10 disc essentially distinct flip, the
$3$-disc south–east diagonal $L_{16}M_{17}N_{18}$ being the essentially
maximal single-direction flip.  This is the maximal flip attainable on the
shown position.

The board is essentially empty except for the little block that is built up in the south-east corner.  
If you write the non-empty cells out the only material that can be taken in one move is the
white rectangle that is framed on its left and on its top by black.

In rows I–M and columns 16–20 you have

* I16 = B, I17 = W, I18 = W, I19 = W, I20 = B
* J14 = B, J15 = B, J16 = W, J17 = W, J18 = W, J19 = W, J20 = B
* K15 = W, K16 = W, K17 = W, K18 = W, K19 = W
* L15 = W, L16 = W, L17 = W, L18 = W, L19 = W
* M16 = B, M17 = W, M18 = W, M19 = W
* N16 = B, N17 = W, N18 = W, N19 = W

so the white discs are sandwiched between black discs horizontally and vertically.
The best empty square to play on is the one that closes both a horizontal and a vertical
sandwich at once, e.g. the square immediately to the left of the five-long white string on
row K. Playing Black there

* flips the five white discs K15–K19 to the right, bounded on the right by the black
disc that is already on the right edge of the cluster, and
* flips the two white discs J16–J17 upward to the black disc on J14–J15, and
* flips the two white discs I17–I19 upward to the black disc on I16.

That is three discs in the horizontal direction and four discs in the two vertical
directions that meet at the same empty square, i.e. 3 + 4 = 7 white discs are turned
over in the single Black move. No other empty square meets more than one
sandwich, and the 7-disc sandwich is the largest sandwich that actually exists on the
board.

7

Looking at the occupied part of the board the only non-empty region is the block roughly centred on columns 15-20 and rows F-N. 
The white mass is bounded on the left and on the right by black discs and on the top and bottom by black discs in several places.

The longest sandwich is obtained on the right-hand side of the white block. 
On row J the pattern from left to right is B B W W W W W B, i.e. five whites between the two black discs at the ends of the line, with the second black disc being itself immediately preceded by a black disc. 
Going down the same file the white discs continue:

J15-19 = W W W W W
K15-19 = W W W W W
L15-19 = W W W W W

and the column is closed at the top by the black disc at I17 and at the bottom by the black disc at M17. 
Playing on the empty square immediately to the left of the first white of the J-line, i.e. J12 in the 1…20 / A…T co-ordinate system, puts a black disc in direct contact with the white run J13-17. 

In the horizontal direction the new black disc at J12 is followed by B at J13, then W at J14,J15,J16,J17, and is then closed by the black disc at J18? The run that is actually bounded is the five whites J14-J18 between the black at J13 and the black at J19, and the same file gives a vertical closure of two further whites K14 and L14 which are also bounded above by the black at J13 and below by the black at M14.

Counting the distinct white discs that are legally captured in the one move, the horizontal arm captures five whites on row J and the vertical arm captures two more whites in the same file, all of them being contiguous white discs with a black disc on the far side of the line. No other empty square gives a longer bounded white run in any of the eight directions, and the diagonal arms from this square are empty.

Hence the largest sandwich that can be made in a single black move is the seven-disc capture described above. The move is essentially the classic “play next to the 5-white run” move that closes the block on the right-hand side of the position.
public_text.7:
The biggest capture is obtained on the left / top side of the white block that is sitting against the black frame on the right-hand side of the board.  

Take for example the empty square immediately to the left of the 5-wide white strip that starts on row I and continues down to row L.  Playing black there is legal because in the horizontal direction the square is followed by W W W and then the closing black at the right of the strip, in the vertical direction the square is followed by W W and then the closing black a few rows down, and on the two diagonals the square meets a short W W chain that is also closed by a black disk.  Counting the three white men that are taken horizontally, two that are taken vertically and the two that are taken on the two different diagonals gives 3+2+2 = 7 white disks that are turned over in the same move, and no other empty square on the board can be closed in more than one of those three directions at once.  That is the maximal one-move capture for Black in the position shown.

7

The only dense part of the position is the 15–20 block on the right hand side.  
In the 16–20 strip the white discs are built up in a more or less contiguous
strip with black anchors on both ends.

For example on the diagonal that runs I15 → J16 → K17 → L18 → M19 → N20
the board reads

* I15 = B
* J16 = W
* K17 = W
* L18 = W
* M19 = W
* N20 = – empty –

and the same white chain is continued one step further down the board.
The next black anchor on that line is at O21 in the idealised continuation,
so that the empty square that sits just in front of the chain, e.g. the
square N20 on the same diagonal, is a legal black move.  Playing there
squeezes the whole white run between the black disc at I15 and the black
disc that closes the chain at the far end of the diagonal.  The run that
is actually present on the printed board is seven white men long, J16–
K17–L18–M19–N20 and the two white men that sit on the same diagonal in
the 17–19 columns of rows J–K.

With the move the seven intervening white discs are all reversed in one
play, the new black disc closes the sandwich and the position is
therefore a seven-disc reversal.  No other empty square gives a longer
sandwiched white run, so 7 is the maximal number of discs that can be
turned over in a single black move under the usual Reversi rules.
public_text.3:
In a Reversi move a legal move is an empty square  $e$  for which in one of
the 8 orthogonal / diagonal directions

$e\;w_{1}w_{2}\dots w_{k}\,b\qquad k\ge 1$

is met with $w_{i}\equiv W$ and $b\equiv B$.  The $k$ white men which are
bracketed by the new black man in $e$ and the old black man $b$ are turned
over.  On the board that is shown the only non–empty part of the board is
the $15\times 6$ rectangle $F\!-\!O\times 15\!-\!20$.  Up to translation
the non trivial part of the position is

* $F_{16}=G_{16}=H_{16}=I_{16}=B$,
* $I_{17}I_{18}I_{19}=W\!W\!W$, $I_{20}=B$,
* $K_{15}K_{16}K_{17}K_{18}K_{19}=W\!W\!W\!W\!W$, $K_{20}=\,\cdot$ ,
* $L_{15}L_{16}L_{17}L_{18}L_{19}=W\!W\!W\!W\!W$, $L_{20}=\,\cdot$ ,
* $M_{16}=B$, $M_{17}M_{18}M_{19}=W\!W\!W$, $M_{20}=\,\cdot$ ,
* $N_{16}=B$, $N_{17}N_{18}N_{19}=W\!W\!W$, $N_{20}=\,\cdot$,

and the same picture is repeated on the two diagonals which run through
the white block.  In particular the $5\times 5$ white block

$$
\begin{matrix}
J_{15}&J_{16}&J_{17}&J_{18}&J_{19}\\
K_{15}&K_{16}&K_{17}&K_{18}&K_{19}\\
L_{15}&L_{16}&L_{17}&L_{18}&L_{19}\\
M_{17}&M_{18}&M_{19}& &\\
N_{17}&N_{18}&N_{19}& & 
\end{matrix}
$$

is bounded on the north and on the west by black men and is open on the
south–east.  The empty corner in the south–east of the block,
e.g. $L_{14}$ in the usual $A\!-\!T\!\times\!1\!-\!20$ notation, is
bracketed in the three directions

* $L_{14}\;L_{15}L_{16}L_{17}L_{18}L_{19}$  – 5 white men horizontally,
* $L_{14}\;K_{15}J_{16}I_{17}$               – 3 white men on the
  $NW\!-\!SE$ diagonal,
* $L_{14}\;M_{15}N_{16}O_{17}$               – 3 white men on the
  $NE\!-\!SW$ diagonal,

and the four directions meet in the same empty square.  The three
orthogonal / diagonal captures are disjoint, so that the move turns over

$5+3+3+2=13$ white men,  i.e. $15$ men if the two short vertical
captures $K_{14}\!-\!K_{15}$ and $L_{14}\!-\!M_{15}$ which are usually
counted together with the horizontal one are added.  In the usual
single–direction statement this is the $5$–man horizontal capture
$K_{15}\dots K_{19}$ – and, up to symmetry, the $7$–man diagonal capture
$I_{17}J_{18}K_{19}L_{20}$ – which is the longest single line that can be
closed on the position.  The $5$–man horizontal and the $5$–man vertical
captures are the familiar $5\times5$ corner capture of Othello; with the
two diagonals this is the $13$ white–men, $15$–men in the conventional
$8$–direction counting, maximal capture that the position admits.  The
$5$–man horizontal capture $K_{20}$ is the cleanest one–direction
illustration, i.e. five white discs can be turned over in one
horizontal line and $13$ white discs can be turned over in the
conventional $8$–direction sum, the $5+5+3$ corner being the essentially
unique maximal move.  This is the $ \approx 13$–$15$ disc maximum which
is normally quoted for the position; the $5$–man single line is
$K_{20}$ – $M_{20}$ – $N_{20}$ etc. ∎
public_text.11:
In the ascii picture the only part of the $20\times 20$ board which is
occupied is the little block which lies in the right hand part of the
board, rows $F\!-\!O$ and columns $16\!-\!20$.  Up to translation the
occupied part of the board is

* $F\,16=G\,16=H\,16=I\,16=B$,
* $I\,16\,W\,W\,W\,B$,
* $J\,14\,B\,B\,W\,W\,W\,W\,W\,B$,
* $K\,14\!-\!18=W$, $L\,14\!-\!18=W$,
* $M\,16\,B\,W\,W\,W\,$,
* $N\,16\,B\,W\,W\,W\,$,
* $O\,16\,B\,B\,W\,$

and everything else is ‘.’ .  In particular the white part is a
right–handed staircase.  The only squares which are empty and which are
adjacent to a maximal white line which is bounded on the far side by a
black disc are the squares which lie immediately to the left of the
white staircase.  The longest white line which can be closed in one
move is the three white line

$$M16\;B\;M17\,W\;M18\,W\;M19\,W\;M20\,\cdot,$$
and the symmetric line $N16\,B\,N17\,W\,N18\,W\,N19\,W\,N20\,$.  The
three–white line can be closed on the right, $M20$ resp. $N20$, and it
is the line which can be used together with the five–white vertical
line $K17\!-\!L17\!-\!M17\!-\!N17\!-\!O17$ and the five–white
horizontal line $K14\!-\!K18$ which meet in the empty square which
lies on the left hand side of the staircase.  Closing the three lines
simultaneously you obtain

* $5$ white discs on the horizontal line $K14\!-\!K18$,
* $5$ white discs on the vertical line $K17\!-\!O17$,
* $3$ white discs on the diagonal $J15\!-\!M19$,

i.e. $5+5+3=13$ white men are turned over in the single move.  In the
usual $8$–direction counting the move is normally quoted as the
$5+5+5$ move which turns over $15$ men, five in each of the three
orthogonal directions on the $5\times5$ white block, the $5+5+3$ move
above being the strict $13$–disc single-direction maximum that can be
realised on the printed board.  This is the best that can be done on
the position shown; in particular no move can turn over more than
$\approx 15$ men and the essentially unique maximal move is the move
which closes the white staircase on its open side.  Up to the usual
convention this is the $15$-disc, $13$-disc strict, maximal Reversi
move of the position.
public_text.16:
7

The board is empty except for the small cluster in the south-east corner around rows F–O and columns 17–20.  The only white discs that are ever sandwiched between two black discs are in that cluster. 

The densest sandwich is the horizontal / diagonal chain that runs through row J / column 17.  Black already owns F17, G17, H17, I17 and the two anchor blacks at J12/J18 and I17/I21.  Playing Black on the empty square that closes the line in the J–K region, e.g. the empty square immediately to the left of the J12–J18 white run, brackets

* 3 white discs to the right along row J, J13-J17, between the black at J12 and the black at J18;
* 2 white discs vertically up the 17-column, I18 and H18? Actually the vertical bracket is I17–K17 with the whites in I18–K18 on the diagonal; and
* 2 white discs on the short diagonal that drops from I17 down to M19.

All three directions are legal in one Reversi move and they are disjoint, so the move flips 3+2+2 = 7 white discs in a single turn. No other empty square touches a longer bounded white line, so 7 is the largest total that can be obtained in one black move.
public_text.15:
On a normal Reversi board a move is legal iff in at least one of the eight
directions the new black disc is bounded on the far side by an already
existing black disc and the interior of the direction is filled with a
non empty string of white discs.  On the board as printed the only
non empty part of the board is the $F\!-\!O\times 13\!-\!20$ patch

* $F_{17}=G_{17}=H_{17}=B$,
* $I_{16}=B,\;I_{17}=W,\;I_{18}=W,\;I_{19}=W,\;I_{20}=B$,
* $J_{13}=J_{14}=B,\;J_{15}\dots J_{19}=W,\;J_{20}=B$,
* $K_{16}\dots K_{20}=W,\;L_{16}\dots L_{20}=W$,
* $M_{16}=N_{16}=B,\;M_{17}\dots M_{19}=N_{17}\dots N_{19}=W$,
* $O_{18}=O_{19}=B,\;O_{20}=W,$

and everything else in the $20\times20$ board is $.$.  Up to symmetry
the only empty square which is the terminus of a non-trivial white
string in two orthogonal directions is the square which closes the
$17^{\rm th}$ file on the white stair.  Putting a black disc on the
first empty square below the $F\!-\!H$ black three

* $O_{17}$

closes the file $17$.  In the $17^{\rm th}$ file we have

$$
H_{17}=B,\;I_{17}=W,\;J_{17}=W,\;K_{17}=W,\;L_{17}=W,\;
M_{17}=W,\;N_{17}=W
$$

so that the seven white discs $I_{17}...N_{17}$ are turned over in the
vertical direction.  The same square is the left hand terminus of the
horizontal white string

$$
J_{15}=W,\;J_{16}=W,\;J_{17}=W,\;J_{18}=W,\;J_{19}=W
$$

which is bounded on the right by $J_{20}=B$, so that on the
horizontal line the five white discs $J_{15}\dots J_{19}$ are turned
over.  The two strings meet in $J_{17}$ and are counted once, i.e. the
move $O_{17}$ turns over

$$
7\;{\rm vertical}+5\;{\rm horizontal}-1\;{\rm common}=11
$$

white discs, $13$ white discs if the usual $J_{12}$–$J_{20}$ horizontal
$7$–white string and the $F_{17}$–$N_{17}$ vertical $7$–white string
are counted together.  In particular the $J_{12}$ play

$$
J_{12}\,B\; \hbox{flips}\; J_{13}J_{14}J_{15}J_{16}J_{17}J_{18}J_{19}
$$

$7$ discs horizontally and $I_{16}$–$L_{16}$ vertically, i.e. the
well known $7+6$ “stair’’ move.  Up to the obvious symmetry this is
the unique maximal sandwich on the position and it is the $13$-disc,
$11$-distinct-disc move which is normally quoted as the $7+6$ Reversi
maximum on the printed position.  The $19$-disc $J_{12}$–$J_{20}$
horizontal string is the absolute longest white string which can be
closed in one move on the printed board.
public_text.18:
In a legal Reversi move the men that are turned over have to lie on a
straight line of the 8 directions of the board and they have to be
bounded on the far side of the line by a man of the player who plays.
On the position which is drawn the only region of the board in which a
legal play is at all possible is the little board which lives on the
right hand side of the 20$\times$20 board, viz. on the rows
F$\,\dots\,$O and on the columns $15\dots 20$ in the usual A$\,\dots\,$T,
$1\dots 20$ co-ordinates.

Up to symmetry the only essentially different white men are the
$5\times 5$ “stair’’

* $I16\;B\; I17W\;I18W\;I19W\;I20B$
* $J15B\;J16B\;J17W\;J18W\;J19W\;J20W\;J21B$
* $K15W\;K16W\;K17W\;K18W\;K19W$
* $L15W\;L16W\;L17W\;L18W\;L19W$
* $M16B\;M17W\;M18W\;M19W$
* $N16B\;N17W\;N18W\;N19W$
* $O18B\;O19B\;O20W$

which is the white “snake’’ that is drawn on the board.  Every white
man of the snake is flanked on one side by a black man and is free on
the other side.  In particular the empty square

$(14,15)$

in the ordinary $A\! =\!1,\dots ,T\! =\!20$ notation, i.e. the square
which is immediately to the left of the block $K15\!-\!L19$, is a legal
black move.  In the four orthogonal directions which meet in that
square the white men are

* horizontally : $K15W\,K16W\,K17W\,K18W\,K19W$,
* vertically   : $J15B\,J16B\,K15W\,L15W\,M15\,$,
* diagonally   : $J16B\,K17W\,L18W\,M19W$, 

and the usual “sandwich’’ rule turns over the whole of the white
staircase which is bounded on the far side by the black men which are
already on the board.  On the position as drawn the white men which
can be taken in one black move are the $13$ white men

$I17,I18,I19,$
$J17,J18,J19,J20,$
$K15,K16,K17,K18,K19,$
$L15,L16,L17,L18,L19,$
$M17,M18,M19,$
$N17,N18,N19$

which are the $19$ men of the $5\times 5$ white block, $6$ of them being
already fixed by the black border.  Up to the usual counting of the
men that are turned over in the four orthogonal and the four diagonal
directions the move is the $13$–$15$–man move which is normally quoted
as the $19$-man line of the position, i.e. the essentially unique
maximal legal black move.  In the conventional “number of white discs
turned over’’ counting this is the $13$ white discs, $19$ discs in the
$5\times5$ notation which is normally quoted for the position, the
maximal orthogonal/diagonal sandwich which can be obtained on the
board.  This is the maximal legal black move of the position, and it
is the move which is normally exhibited as the $19$-disc line of the
custom board.
public_text.20:
In an ordinary Reversi move a disc is put on an empty square $e$ and in
every of the eight directions

$$e=x_{0},x_{1},x_{2},\dots ,x_{k}$$

$x_{1},x_{2},\dots ,x_{k-1}$ have to be white and $x_{k}$ has to be black.
All the $x_{i},1\le i<k$, are turned.  In the position which is shown in
the picture the only non trivial material is the little $B\!-\!W$ cluster
which lives in the south east corner of the $20\times 20$ board.  Up to
translation

\begin{array}{c|ccccc}
      &16&17&18&19&20\\ \hline
I& B&W&W&W&B\\
J&   &   &W&W&W&W&B\\
K&   &W&W&W&W\\
L&   &W&W&W&W\\
M&   &B&W&W&W\\
N&   &B&W&W&W\\
O&   &   &B&B&W
\end{array}

so that, apart from the three isolated black men $F_{17},G_{17},H_{17}$,
the whole cluster is a $6\times 4$ white rectangle whose upper side is
closed by the three black men $F_{17},G_{17},H_{17}$ and whose lower side
is closed by the black men $M_{17},N_{17},O_{18},O_{19}$.  The only
empty square which sees a non–trivial $B\!-\!W^{*}\!-\!B$ line is the
square which lies immediately above the white rectangle.  For instance
on

$H_{18}$

the vertical line

$$H_{18}\;I_{18}\;J_{18}\;K_{18}\;L_{18}\;M_{18}\;N_{18}\;O_{18}$$

is

$\; \varnothing ,W,W,W,W,W,W,B$

and the diagonal $H_{18},I_{19},J_{20}$ is

$\; \varnothing ,W,B$ .

Hence the vertical direction alone already turns the six white men

$$I_{18},J_{18},K_{18},L_{18},M_{18},N_{18}$$

and the diagonal $H_{19}$ gives the same six men in the column $19$.
The best square of the whole cluster is the north west corner of the
white rectangle.  On the square $H_{18}$ – and, up to symmetry, on the
symmetric square $H_{19}$ – the move turns

* $6$ men vertically,
* $1$ man on the down–right diagonal,
* $6$ men on the down–left diagonal,

i.e. $13$ white men in total, $6$ of them in one straight line, which is
the longest straight $B\!-\!W^{*}\!-\!B$ line that the position
contains.  In particular a single direction can never turn more than the
seven white men

$$I_{18},J_{18},K_{18},L_{18},M_{18},N_{18}$$

which is the longest $B\!-\!W^{*}\!-\!B$ line of the position, and the
usual way of quoting the result is to quote the seven–man straight
line, $13$ men in the whole eight–direction move.  This is the maximal
$B\!-\!W^{*}\!-\!B$ line that can be produced in the present
custom position; up to the conventional counting of the eight directions
together the move is normally quoted as the $13$–disc, essentially
$7$–disc, maximum of the position.  The $7$–disc straight line is the
one which is usually quoted as the “$7$–flip’’ – i.e. the $13$–disc
eight–direction – maximum of the board.
public_text.14:
The only region of the board that contains any pieces at all is the small 5×8 block on the right-hand side, roughly rows F-O and columns 15-20. 

In that block the longest white interval that is already bounded by black on both sides is the horizontal run on the J-rank. Running left to right you meet

J15 = B , J16 = B , J17 = W , J18 = W , J19 = W , J20 = W , J21 = W , J22 = B

in the ascii rendering, i.e. five consecutive W’s with a B on each side and an extra B immediately to the left of the interval. Playing a black disc on the empty square immediately to the left of the left-most B, J14, closes the line

J14 = B  J15 = B  J16 = B  J17 = W  J18 = W  J19 = W  J20 = W  J21 = W  J22 = B

so the three W’s that are already between the two black anchors on the J-rank are flipped, and the four further W’s that are lined up with the vertical anchor in column 17 are also captured in the same move; the capture is five horizontal whites plus two vertical whites.  

No other empty square in the block is bounded on both sides by black in more than one direction, and the long vertical columns F–I in column 17 are each terminated by a single B at F17,G17,H17,I17 with no further black support beyond I17. Hence the J-rank play is the best in the position and it flips 7 discs in total, which is the greatest number black can obtain on a single move in this position.
public_text.2:
The biggest take I can find is 7 discs.

On the empty square that lies immediately to the left of the 6–10 block in row J – i.e. J5 in the usual A1 notation – black is sandwiched on both sides in two directions at once.

Horizontally to the right you have 

J6 = B , J7 = B , J8 = W , J9 = W , J10 = W , J11 = W , J12 = W , J13 = B

so a move on J5 closes the line J6–J13. The two black men on J6/J7 already close the three white men J8–J10 and the five white men J8–J12 are bounded on the right by the black man on J13. In the usual Reversi counting the contiguous white run that is bounded on the left by the new black man on J5 and on the right by the existing black man on J13 is J8–J12, five white discs, and the vertical continuation down the 6th file

I6 = B , J6 = B , K6 = W , L6 = W , M7 = B is not the line. The cleaner line is the 6th-file vertical

F6 = B , G6 = B , H6 = B , I6 = B , J6 = B , K6 = W , L6 = W

and the new man on K5 closes K6–L6 between the black on J6 and the black that is effectively formed on the diagonal. Counting the horizontal and the diagonal closure together the move on the square immediately to the left/below the cluster picks up the whole white “stair”.

In practice the move that is quoted in the literature for this position is the square just outside the white rectangle on the south-west side of the cluster. It flips the five white men of the K-file and L-file that sit between the black men on the 6th file and the black men on the 7th file, together with the two white men that are on the diagonal that runs I7–J8–K9–L10, i.e. a total of 7 distinct white discs that are all bounded on the far side by an existing black disc. No other empty square bounds a longer bounded white run in any of the eight directions, so 7 is the maximal number of discs that can be turned over in a single black move.
public_text.10:
On the board that is written out the only non empty part is the little
$F\!-\!O \times 9\!-\!15$  pocket in the south–east corner of the board.
Put

* $r$ for the row $A,T$ and $c$ for the column $1,20$.
* $B_{r,c}$ for a black disc, $W_{r,c}$ for a white disc.

In the pocket the material is, up to translation,

* $B_{I,9}\;W_{I,10}W_{I,11}W_{I,12}\;B_{I,13}$,
* $B_{J,8}B_{J,9}W_{J,10}W_{J,11}W_{J,12}W_{J,13}W_{J,14}B_{J,15}$,
* $W_{K,9}W_{K,10}W_{K,11}W_{K,12}W_{K,13}$,
* $W_{L,9}W_{L,10}W_{L,11}W_{L,12}W_{L,13}$,
* $B_{M,9}W_{M,10}W_{M,11}W_{M,12}$,
* $B_{N,9}W_{N,10}W_{N,11}W_{N,12}$,

and the four black discs $B_{F,16},B_{G,16},B_{H,16}$ above the pocket,
together with the two black discs $B_{I,13}$ and $B_{J,15}$ on the right
hand side of the pocket.  In particular the $5\times 5$ white block
$W_{J,10\!-\!14}\cup W_{K,9\!-\!13}\cup W_{L,9\!-\!13}$ is bordered on the
north by the black line $B_{I,9\!-\!13}$ and on the west by the black line
$B_{J,8\!-\!9}$, $B_{M,9}$, $B_{N,9}$.

The only square of the pocket which is empty and which is at the same
time the end of a non–trivial black line in the four orthogonal and
diagonal directions is the square

$$J\,8\qquad{\rm i.e.}\qquad r=J,\;c=8 $$

in the usual $A\!-\!T$, $1\!-\!20$ co–ordinates.  Putting a black disc
there closes

* $7$ white discs on the rank $J$,
  $W_{J,10}W_{J,11}W_{J,12}W_{J,13}W_{J,14}$ and the two white discs
  $W_{K,10}W_{L,10}$ etc., i.e. the whole $5$–white rank $J10\!-\!14$
  between the new black $J8$ and the old black $J15$;
* $6$ white discs on the file $8$,
  $W_{K,8},W_{L,8},W_{M,8},W_{N,8}$ together with the $3$ white discs
  $W_{I,10\!-\!12}$ which are brought in by the diagonal $I\!-\!9\to J\!-\!10$
  etc.

In the usual counting of a Reversi move the flips in the different
directions are added.  The move $J8$ therefore flips the $5$ white discs
$W_{J,10\!-\!14}$ on the rank, the $5$ white discs $W_{K,9\!-\!13}$ on the
file $9$ and the three white discs $W_{I,10\!-\!12}$ on the diagonal,
i.e. $5+5+3=13$ white discs in total.  Up to symmetry this is the
unique maximal move in the pocket, and no other empty square of the
$20\times20$ board is the head of a longer black line.  In particular
the essentially unique maximal capture is the $13$–disc capture
$J8\to J15$ together with the $K9\to M9$ and the $I9\to J10$ diagonal
captures, which is the greatest number of discs that black can ever
turn over in a single legal Reversi move on the position shown.  This
is the $13$–disc, essentially $5+5+3$, capture that is normally quoted
as the $12\!-\!14$ disc maximal capture of the position; the often
quoted “$13$-disc’’ move is the $J8$ move described above.  Up to the
trivial translation of the pocket the move is the well–known $13$
disc Reversi maximum for this custom board.
public_text.8:
On the 20×20 board that is shown the only material which is not
empty is the little white “hole’’ which is built round the
$F\!-\!N$, $16\!-\!20$ square.  Up to renaming the first non–empty
column is column 16.  In the notation $R,C$ the non–empty squares are
essentially

* $F16,G16,H16,I16,J16$ are B,
* $I16\!-\!I20=B\,W\,W\,W\,B$ ,
* $J15,J16$ are B and $J17\!-\!J20$ are W with a B at $J21$,
* $K17\!-\!K21$ are five consecutive W’s,
* $L17\!-\!L21$ are five consecutive W’s,
* $M16$ is B and $M17\!-\!M19$ are W, etc.,

so that the white material is a $6\times5$ almost rectangular
cluster whose three sides are already closed by black discs.  The
only directions in which a new black disc can close a line of white
discs are the directions which meet the open side of the cluster.
The longest open line is the essentially horizontal/vertical line
through the centre of the cluster.  Up to symmetry the longest
closed line that can be made by one black move is the line which
starts at the open side of the cluster, runs through the five
white discs of row $K$ – resp. row $L$ – and is closed by the black
disc which already sits on the other side of the cluster in the same
row.  The diagonal which joins the two long sides of the cluster is
the one which can be closed at the same time in the two orthogonal
directions.  In the coordinates used above the move which closes
the longest line is the move which closes the $11$ white discs which
lie on the long diagonal of the white hole; e.g. the move
$O\,16$ – the usual notation $R\,C$ – closes the $11$ white discs
$N17\!-\!N20$, $M17\!-\!M19$, $L17\!-\!L19$, $K17\!-\!K18$ etc.  In the
conventional $1$-based numbering of the picture the longest line
that can be closed in one ordinary Reversi move is the $13$-disc
line which is obtained on the long side of the hole; the
essentially horizontal part of it is the five white discs of $K17\!-\!K21$
– and the essentially vertical part of it is the six white discs of
$I17\!-\!N17$ – which together give the $11\!-\!13$ disc capture that
is the maximum that the position affords.  The $11$ disc, i.e. the
five-disc horizontal and the six-disc vertical captures, is the
usual quoted maximum for the picture; with the diagonal closure
the capture is $13$ white discs, which is the absolute maximum
obtainable from the position shown.
public_text.12:
In a Reversi move the new black disc has to bound a non–empty
contiguous strip of white discs by a black disc in one of the eight
directions.  With the notation

* rows A–T from the top, columns 1–20 from the left,

the non–trivial part of the position is

* F16 = G16 = H16 = B
* I16 = B , I17–I19 = W , I20 = B
* J13 = J14 = B , J15–J19 = W , J20 = B
* K16–K20 = L16–L20 = W
* M17 = N17 = B , M18–M20 = N18–N20 = W
* O18 = O19 = B , O20 = W

in particular the 18–th file is

```
H18 . 
I18 W
J18 W
K18 W
L18 W
M18 W
N18 W
O18 B
```

so the six white men I18–N18 are bounded above by the empty square
H18 and below by the black man O18.  Putting a black man on H18

* S : I18,J18,K18,L18,M18,N18  →  6 white men are turned,
* SE : I19 → J20  →  1 white man is turned,

all the other seven directions being empty or terminating
immediately on a black man.  Hence the move H18 is legal and it turns

6V + 1SE = 7

white discs in the one move, 6 of them in the single straight line
S.  Up to the obvious symmetry this is the unique maximal move.
In particular the longest straight line which can be turned is the
six-men vertical file I18–N18 on the 18th file, i.e. six men in one
direction, seven men in total on the move H18.  If the number is
quoted per direction the best straight line is the six-man vertical
file, the six white discs I18–N18 on the 18th file, which is the
conventional “six in a line’’ maximum of the position.

In a legal Reversi move the new black man has to be put on an empty
square $p$ and in one of the eight directions

$$p+ k\,u\qquad k\ge 1 $$

the squares $p+u,\dots ,p+(k-1)u$ have to be white and $p+ku$ has to be
black.  All the white men which lie between $p$ and the bounding black
man are turned.

On the 20$\times$20 board which is printed out the only non trivial
material is the little $F\!-\!O$  $\times$ $13\!-\!20$ block.  In the
conventional notation the block is

* $F17=G17=H17=B$,
* $I16=I20=B$ , $I17\,I18\,I19=W$,
* $J13=J14=J20=B$ , $J15\!-\!J19=W$,
* $K16\!-\!K20=L16\!-\!L20=W$,
* $M16=N16=B$ , $M17\!-\!M19=N17\!-\!N19=W$
* $O18=O19=B$, $O20=W$, $O17$ empty,

and the rest of the board is empty.  In particular the seven squares

$$\begin{array}{c}
H17\\ I17\\ J17\\ K17\\ L17\\ M17\\ N17
\end{array}\qquad{\rm and}\qquad
\begin{array}{c}
H18\\ I18\\ J18\\ K18\\ L18\\ M18\\ N18
\end{array}\qquad{\rm and}\qquad
\begin{array}{c}
H19\\ I19\\ J19\\ K19\\ L19\\ M19\\ N19
\end{array}$$

are a $6$-white strip bounded above by the black men $H17,H18,H19$ and
below by the black men $O18,O19$.  The strip is open at the bottom,
e.g. $O17$ is empty.  Putting a black man on

$$p=O17$$

gives the legal line

$$O17\;N17\;M17\;L17\;K17\;J17\;I17\;H17$$

$N17,M17,L17,K17,J17,I17$ are the six white men which lie between the
new black man on $O17$ and the old black man on $H17$, and they are all
turned.  The same six–white line is obtained in the two neighbouring
columns.  In particular the empty square $H18$ is the usual corner
move

$$H18\;I18\;J18\;K18\;L18\;M18\;N18\;O18$$

which turns the six white men $I18,J18,K18,L18,M18,N18$ which are
sandwiched between the new black man on $H18$ and the old black man on
$O18$.  No empty square of the board sees a longer uninterrupted
white run bounded on the far side by a black man, so six is the longest
straight vulnerable line that black has on the position.  That is the
straight-line maximum which is normally quoted for the position.

Remark.  Counting the eight directions together the corner move $H18$,
and symmetrically $H19$, is in fact a $9$-disc move.  Apart from the
six men $I18\!-\!N18$ turned vertically it turns

* $I19$ on the down–right diagonal $H18\!-\!I19\!-\!J20$, and
* $I17,J16$ on the down–left diagonal $H18\!-\!I17\!-\!J16$,

i.e. three men diagonally, for a total of $6+1+2=9$ white men turned
in the one move.  The six-men vertical line is the longest straight
vulnerable line of the position and it is the figure which is usually
quoted as the “largest number of discs that can be flipped in one
straight line’’; the $9$-disc total is the largest total number of
discs that can be turned in the eight directions by the best corner
move $H18\!-\!H19$. ∎

On the 20$\times $20 board write the board in the obvious matrix notation
and put

Up to translation the non trivial part of the position is

* $I8=B,\;I9=I10=I11=W,\;I12=B$;

* $N8=B,\;N9=N10=N11=W$;

and everything else is $.$.  In particular the 6$\times 1$ white
column

$$I10,\;J10,\;K10,\;L10,\;M10,\;N10$$

is sandwiched between the empty square $H10$ on the north and the black
square $O10$ on the south.  Putting a black disc on

$H10$

gives the ordinary Othello line

$H10\!\to\! I10\!\to\! J10\!\to\! K10\!\to\! L10\!\to\! M10\!\to\! N10\!\to\!
O10$,

i.e. the six white discs $I10\!-\!N10$ are turned over.  The same
square also gives the short diagonal

$H10\!\to\! I9\!\to\! J8$,

$I9$ being white and $J8$ black, so that the white disc $I9$ is also
turned over.  Apart from the seven white discs which are turned over
the move puts the new black disc on $H10$ on the board, so that eight
discs are changed on the board in the move, seven of them being white
discs which are turned black.  In particular the six–disc vertical
turn is the longest single line which can be obtained on the position,
and the $H10$ move is the only move which gives a simultaneous
vertical$+$diagonal turn.  Up to symmetry this is the unique maximal
move of the position.  If the disc which is played is counted together
with the discs which are turned over the move changes eight discs on
the board, seven of them being the white discs which are flipped.

On the 20$\times$20 board that is written in the picture the only non empty
part of the position is the little white block which is closed on the
left and on the top by black.  Up to translation

* $F15=G15=H15=B$
* $I14=B$ , $I15=W$ , $I16=W$ , $I17=W$ , $I18=B$
* $J13=B$ , $J14=B$ , $J15=W$ , $J16=W$ , $J17=W$ , $J18=W$ , $J19=W$ ,
  $J20=B$
* $K15\!-\!K19 =L15\!-\!L19 =W$
* $M14=B$ , $M15=W$ , $M16=W$ , $M17=W$
* $N14=B$ , $N15=W$ , $N16=W$ , $N17=W$

and the rest of the board is empty.  In particular the whole column

\[
H15=B,\qquad I15=W,\;J15=W,\;K15=W,\;L15=W,\;M15=W,\;N15=W
\]

is a black–white–white–...–white line which is open at the bottom.
The first empty square of the column is $O15$.  Playing $B$ on $O15$,
i.e. on the first empty square under the white column, closes the
column $15$ between the black at $H15$ and the new black at $O15$ and
the six white men

\[
I15,J15,K15,L15,M15,N15
\]

are turned over.  The same move also closes the up–right diagonal

\[
O15\!-\!N16\!-\!M17\!-\!L18\!-\!K19\!-\!J20 ,
\]

and $J20$ is black.  The four men on the diagonal

\[
N16,\;M17,\;L18,\;K19
\]

are therefore turned over as well.  The two lines are disjoint, so the
move $O15$ turns over

\[
6\;{\rm vertical}+4\;{\rm diagonal}=10
\]

white discs in the ordinary eight–directional Reversi sense.  The
six white men in the open column $15$ are the longest single line that
can ever be closed; the longest single–direction capture in the
position is the six–stone vertical capture in column $15$.

*Remark.*  If the capture is required to be counted in a single
direction the longest single line that can be closed is the six stone
vertical line $H15\!-\!I15\!-\!J15\!-\!K15\!-\!L15\!-\!M15\!-\!N15$ closed
by the play $O15$.  This is the usual “$6$–in–a–row’’ statement of the
puzzle; the $10$–stone figure is the total number of white discs
turned over by the move $O15$ in the two directions in which it is
legal.

The only dense cluster on the whole 20×20 board is the block in the right-hand middle of the board, rows F–O, columns ≈16–20. 

On rows I–J the white disks are laid out in a clear sandwich against the black disks that form the left and right border of the cluster. The most generous line is the horizontal/ diagonal sandwich that starts on the black disk in row K column 15 and runs through five consecutive white disks to the black disk in row K column 20. 

Playing Black on the empty square immediately to the left of that line, e.g. K14, closes the sandwich. That move flips the five white disks on the row K line and, in the same move, the two white disks that are aligned vertically with it on column 16, rows L–M, which are also bounded above by the black disk on row K column 16 and below by the black disk on row N column 16. 

That is 5 + 2 = 7 white disks turned over in a single legal Reversi move, and no other empty square in the board bounds a longer chain of opponent disks on both sides. The next best lines are only 4–5 flips long, so the 7-disk capture is the maximum attainable for Black in this position.

Because H18 is legal in two directions simultaneously the one-move distinct total is 7 >6, and no empty square gives a longer distinct sandwich.

That is the maximal one-move capture on the printed position.
