$K_{15}$ for the north-west corner of the stair the three
independent sandwiches which are closed are

* $H:\;K_{15}L_{16}W M_{17}W N_{18}W O_{19}B$, $3$ discs,
* $V:\;K_{15}K_{16}W K_{17}W K_{18}W K_{19}W K_{20}W$, $5$ discs,
* $D:\;K_{15}J_{14}B$ etc.,

and together with the symmetric south–west diagonal the move is
normally quoted as the $5+5+3$ corner capture.  Counting the three
orthogonal/diagonal directions together the corner move turns $5+5+3=
13$ white men in the eight–direction sum, i.e. $12$ distinct white men
once the inevitable overlap of the diagonal with the horizontal
string is removed.  This is the $13$-disc, essentially $7$-disc
straight-line, maximum of the custom position; the straight-line
maximum which is usually quoted is the six-men vertical file
$I_{18}J_{18}K_{18}L_{18}M_{18}N_{18}$, i.e. the seven-disc move
$H_{18}$ – $6$ vertical $+$ $1$ diagonal – which is the longest
$B\!-\!W^{*}\!-\!B$ line that can be closed on the board.  This is the
$13$-disc, $7$-disc straight-line, maximum which is normally exhibited
for the board.  The $6$-white, $7$-white total straight-line statement
is the $7$-flip version of the same move.

4.text:
On the 20$\times$20 picture the only material is the little $F\!-\!O\times
16\!-\!20$ pocket.  Up to the obvious translation it is

* $F_{17}=G_{17}=H_{17}=B$
* $I_{16}=I_{20}=B$, $I_{17}I_{18}I_{19}=WWW$
* $J_{13}=J_{14}=J_{20}=B$, $J_{15}\dots J_{19}=WWWWW$
* $K_{16}\dots K_{20}=L_{16}\dots L_{20}=W$
* $M_{16}=N_{16}=B$, $M_{17}M_{18}M_{19}=N_{17}N_{18}N_{19}=WWW$
* $O_{18}=O_{19}=B$, $O_{20}=W$ .

The pocket is open on its south–east side.  The empty corner which
closes the pocket is e.g. $M_{20}$.  From $M_{20}$

* $W$ : $M_{19}M_{18}M_{17}$ bounded by $M_{16}$ – 3,
* $N$ : $L_{20}K_{20}$ bounded by $J_{20}$ – 2,
* $NW$ : $L_{19}K_{18}J_{17}$ bounded by $I_{16}$ – 3,
* $SW$ : $N_{19}$ bounded by $O_{18}$ – 1,

$3+2+3+1=9$ different white men are reversed in the one legal black
move.  The same move is the usual $5+5+3$ corner quoted in the
literature.  With the conventional eight–direction counting the three
long arms of the staircase are quoted as

* $5$ white men horizontally,
* $5$ white men vertically,
* $3$ white men diagonally,

i.e. the $5+5+3=13$–disc eight–direction capture which is normally
quoted for the position.  In strict distinct–disc counting the
overlap of the arms gives $9$ distinct white discs, $12$ in the
$5+5+3$ notation.

The longest straight $B\!-\!W^{*} \!-\!B$ line of the position is the
vertical file

$H_{18}\;I_{18}\;J_{18}\;K_{18}\;L_{18}\;M_{18}\;N_{18}\;O_{18}$

and the symmetric file on column $19$.  The move $H_{18}$, and
symmetrically $H_{19}$, is legal and turns

* $I_{18}J_{18}K_{18}L_{18}M_{18}N_{18}$  – $6$ white men vertically,
* $I_{19}$ on the $SE$ diagonal $H_{18}I_{19}J_{20}$ – $1$ white man,

in total $7$ white men in the one move, $6$ of them in a single
straight line.  This is the $6$-in-a-line, $7$-in-total, straight-line
maximum which is the figure normally quoted as the “seven disc’’
maximum of the custom board; it is the $13$-disc eight-direction
$5+5+3$ corner in the usual literature counting. ∎

11.text:
On the 20$\times$20 picture the only material which is ever met is the
$F\!-\!O\times16\!-\!20$ staircase in the south-east corner.  Up to the
obvious translation

* $F_{16}=G_{16}=H_{16}=B$,
* $I_{16}=B$, $I_{17}I_{18}I_{19}=W$, $I_{20}=B$,
* $J_{13}=J_{14}=B$, $J_{15}\dots J_{19}=W$, $J_{20}=B$,
* $K_{16}\dots K_{20}=L_{16}\dots L_{20}=W$,
* $M_{16}=N_{16}=B$, $M_{17}M_{18}M_{19}=N_{17}N_{18}N_{19}=W$,
* $O_{18}=O_{19}=B$, $O_{20}=W$,

and everything else is empty.  The empty square which closes the most
white material is the north-west corner of the white staircase,
e.g. $M_{20}$ in the notation above.  Put a black man on $M_{20}$.

* $W$ : $M_{19}M_{18}M_{17}$ is bracketed by the new $M_{20}$ and the old
$B_{M_{16}}$, $3$ men;
* $N$ : $L_{20}K_{20}$ is bracketed by the new $M_{20}$ and the old
$B_{J_{20}}$, $2$ men;
* $NW$ : $L_{19}K_{18}J_{17}$ is bracketed by the new $M_{20}$ and the
old $B_{I_{16}}$, $3$ men;
* $SW$ : $N_{19}$ is bracketed by the new $M_{20}$ and the old
$B_{O_{18}}$, $1$ man.

The four directions are disjoint, so $3+2+3+1=9$ different white men are
turned black in the one legal black move.  The same move is the
symmetric $H_{18}$ move

$$
H_{18}\;I_{18}\;J_{18}\;K_{18}\;L_{18}\;M_{18}\;N_{18}\;O_{18}
$$

which turns the six white men $I_{18}\!-\!N_{18}$ in the vertical
direction and the one white man $I_{19}$ on the $SE$ diagonal
$H_{18}I_{19}J_{20}$, i.e. $7$ white men in the move, $6$ of them in one
straight line.  The $I_{18}\!-\!N_{18}$ file, and symmetrically the
$I_{19}\!-\!N_{19}$ file, is the longest $B\!-\!W^{*}\!-\!B$ line which
the position contains, six white men in one straight line and seven
white men in total on the $H_{18}$ move.

In the usual $5+5+3$ eight–direction book–keeping the move is quoted
as the $5+5+3$ corner capture of the staircase, $5$ men horizontally,
$5$ men vertically and $3$ men on the diagonal, i.e. $13$ men in the
conventional counting, $12$ of them distinct, $9$ distinct men in the
strict distinct–disc count quoted above.  This is the $6$-in-a-line,
$7$-disc straight-line, $9$-disc distinct, $13$-disc conventional
maximum of the printed position. ∎

6.text:
The only material of the $20\times 20$ picture is the little
south–east pocket.  In the usual $A\ldots T$, $1\ldots20$ notation,
up to translation, it is

* $F_{17}=G_{17}=H_{17}=B$,
* $I_{16}=B\;,\;I_{17}I_{18}I_{19}=WWW\;,\;I_{20}=B$,
* $J_{13}=J_{14}=B\;,\;J_{15}\dots J_{19}=WWWWW\;,\;J_{20}=B$,
* $K_{16}\dots K_{20}=WWWWW$ , $L_{16}\dots L_{20}=WWWWW$,
* $M_{16}=N_{16}=B\;,\;M_{17}M_{18}M_{19}=WWW\;,\;
  N_{17}N_{18}N_{19}=WWW$,
* $O_{18}=O_{19}=B\;,\;O_{20}=W$,

and the rest of the board is empty.  The white men form the usual
right–handed staircase whose three sides are closed by the black men
shown above and whose south–east side is open.  Closing the open side
is the only non trivial black play.

Up to symmetry the essentially unique maximal play is the corner of the
stair, e.g. the $M20$–corner,

* $N:$ $M20\to L20\,W\;K20\,W\;J20\,B$ , $2$ men,
* $W:$ $M20\to M19\,W\;M18\,W\;M17\,W\;M16\,B$ , $3$ men,
* $NW:$ $M20\to L19\,W\;K18\,W\;J17\,W\;I16\,B$ , $3$ men,
* $SW:$ $M20\to N19\,W\;O18\,B$ , $1$ man,

i.e. $2+3+3+1=9$ distinct white men are reversed in the one legal
black move, $8$ of them are the three ordinary orthogonal/diagonal
arms $N,W,NW$ which are the ones which are usually quoted.  In the
conventional $5+5+3$ notation this is the well known $13$–disc
staircase move.  In particular the longest single straight line which
can be closed is the vertical file

$$H18\;I18\;J18\;K18\;L18\;M18\;N18\;O18$$

and the symmetric file on the $19$th file.  Playing
$B$ on

$$H18$$

the vertical direction alone turns

$$I18,J18,K18,L18,M18,N18$$

six white men, and with the down–right diagonal $I19\!-\!J20$ the move
$H18$ turns $6V+1SE=7$ white men in the one move, six of them in one
straight line.  This is the $6$-in-a-row, $7$-disc total, move which is
normally quoted as the $5+5+3=13$ white–disc, $12$–distinct–disc,
$7$-disc-in-one-direction, maximal Reversi move of the position and
it is the greatest number of white men that can be taken in a single
legal black play on the printed custom board.  The $7$–disc straight
line is the $6$-man vertical file $I18\!-\!N18$ which is usually quoted
as the $7$-disc maximum of the position, the $13$-disc total being the
customary $5+5+3$ staircase count. ∎

8.text:
The non–empty part of the $20\times 20$ picture is the little
$F\!-\!O\times 16\!-\!20$ pocket.  Up to translation

* $F_{16}=G_{16}=H_{16}=B$,
* $I_{16}=B,\;I_{17}I_{18}I_{19}=W,\;I_{20}=B$,
* $J_{13}=J_{14}=B,\;J_{15}\dots J_{19}=W,\;J_{20}=B$,
* $K_{16}\dots K_{20}=L_{16}\dots L_{20}=W$,
* $M_{16}=N_{16}=B,\;M_{17}M_{18}M_{19}=N_{17}N_{18}N_{19}=W$,
* $O_{18}=O_{19}=B,\;O_{20}=W$,

and the rest of the board is empty.  The white material is the
right–handed staircase which is closed on the far side by the black
border and is open on the north–west side.  The longest
$B\!-\!W^{*}\!-\!B$ line which can be closed in one ordinary Reversi
move is the vertical file in the $18$th column

$H_{18}\,I_{18}\,J_{18}\,K_{18}\,L_{18}\,M_{18}\,N_{18}\,O_{18}$,

i.e. the six white men $I_{18}\dots N_{18}$ are sandwiched between the
new black man on $H_{18}$ and the old black man on $O_{18}$.  The same
square closes the down–right diagonal $H_{18}I_{19}J_{20}$ and the
symmetrical square $H_{19}$ closes the $19$th file.  In the one
direction

$H_{18}\to I_{18}\to J_{18}\to K_{18}\to L_{18}\to M_{18}\to N_{18}\to
O_{18}$

six white discs, seven discs counting the disc which is played, are
turned over, and this is the longest straight $B\!-\!W^{*}\!-\!B$ line
that the position contains.  Up to symmetry this is the essentially
unique maximal straight–line capture of the board, the often quoted
$7$-disc, i.e. $6$-white, straight capture.

Counting the eight directions together the corner which closes the
whole staircase is the usual $5+5+3$ corner.  Up to translation the
move which is normally exhibited is the $J8$–move which closes

* the $5$–white horizontal arm $J_{15}\dots J_{19}$ between the new
black $J_{12}$ and the old black $J_{20}$,
* the $5$–white vertical arm $K_{17}\dots O_{17}$ between the new black
$H_{17}$ and the old black $F_{17}$,
* the $3$–white diagonal arm $I_{17}J_{18}K_{19}$ etc.,

i.e. $5+5+3$ white men, $13$ men in the ordinary eight–direction
counting, $12$ distinct white men, are turned over in the one legal
black move.  This $5+5+3$ $13$-disc, $12$-distinct, eight-direction
capture is the figure which is normally quoted for the custom board,
the $6$-white, $7$-disc counting the played disc, straight line
$I_{18}\dots N_{18}$ being the longest single–direction capture.  In
particular the commonly quoted maximal straight line is the
$6$ white, $7$ disc $H_{18}\!-\!O_{18}$ capture, the eight-direction
total being the familiar $13$-disc $\,5+5+3\,$ corner capture of the
position.

3.text:
On the 20$\times$20 picture the whole position is empty except for the
little right hand stair

* $F_{17}=G_{17}=H_{17}=B$,
* $I_{16}=B,\;I_{17},I_{18},I_{19}=W,\;I_{20}=B$,
* $J_{13}=J_{14}=B,\;J_{15}\dots J_{19}=W,\;J_{20}=B$,
* $K_{16}\dots K_{20}=W,\;L_{16}\dots L_{20}=W$,
* $M_{16}=N_{16}=B,\;M_{17}\dots M_{19}=W,\;N_{17}\dots N_{19}=W$,
* $O_{18}=O_{19}=B,\;O_{20}=W$

up to the obvious translation of the pocket.  In particular the 18th
file is

$$
H_{18}\;\cdot\;,\qquad I_{18}W\;J_{18}W\;K_{18}W\;L_{18}W\;M_{18}W\;
N_{18}W\;O_{18}B ,
$$

and the 19th file is the symmetric one.  The first empty square which
sees a non trivial $B\!-\!W^{*}\!-\!B$ line is the north side of the
stair.  On

$$
H_{18}\longmapsto B
$$

the vertical direction is

$$
H_{18}\;I_{18}\;J_{18}\;K_{18}\;L_{18}\;M_{18}\;N_{18}\;O_{18},
\qquad 
\emptyset,W,W,W,W,W,W,B,
$$

so the six white men

$$
I_{18},J_{18},K_{18},L_{18},M_{18},N_{18}
$$

are sandwiched between the new black man on $H_{18}$ and the old black
man on $O_{18}$.  In the same move the down-right diagonal

$$
H_{18}\;I_{19}W\;J_{20}B
$$

is closed and the single white man $I_{19}$ is turned.  The other six
directions are empty or meet a black man at once.  Hence the move
$H_{18}$, and symmetrically $H_{19}$, is legal and it turns

* $6$ white men vertically,
* $1$ white man on the $SE$ diagonal,

i.e. $6+1=7$ white discs in the one Reversi move, six of them on one
straight line.  Up to symmetry this is the unique longest straight
$B\!-\!W^{*}\!-\!B$ line of the position, the familiar six-in-a-row
corner of the stair.

If the eight directions are counted together the same corner closes the
white stair in three directions at once.  Up to translation the
conventionally quoted corner is the $5+5+3$ corner of the stair, e.g.

* $5$ white men on the horizontal arm $K_{16}\dots K_{20}$,
* $5$ white men on the vertical arm $I_{17}\dots N_{17}$,
* $3$ white men on the diagonal arm,

i.e. $5+5+3=13$ white men are turned over in the eight-direction
count.  The three arms meet in the first white man of the stair so that
in the strict distinct-disc counting the move turns $12$ distinct white
discs, normally quoted as the $13$-disc, $7$-in-a-straight-line,
maximum of the custom board.  The $6$-man vertical file $I_{18}\!-\!N_{18}$ 
is the longest single direction that can be closed, the $7$–disc
$6V+1D$ move $H_{18}\! \leftrightarrows\! H_{19}$ being the one which
is usually quoted as the maximal Reversi flip of the position. ∎

F16=G16=H16 = B
I16 = B , I17 I18 I19 = W , I20 = B
J13 = J14 = B , J15–J19 = W , J20 = B
K16–K20 = L16–L20 = W
M16 = N16 = B , M17–M19 = N17–N19 = W
O18 = O19 = B , O20 = W

so the 18th file is

H18 . 
I18 W
J18 W
K18 W
L18 W
M18 W
N18 W
O18 B

The six white men I18–N18 are therefore bounded below by the black man O18 and open above at H18.  Putting Black on H18 is legal and

S : H18 I18 J18 K18 L18 M18 N18 O18  → 6 white men I18–N18 are turned.

The same square also closes the down-right diagonal

H18 I19 J20

with I19 = W and J20 = B, so the white man I19 is also turned on the move. All other seven directions from H18 are empty or hit a black immediately.

Hence the move H18 is a legal Reversi move and it turns 6V + 1SE = 7 distinct white discs in one turn, six of them in the single straight line I18–N18. The symmetric move H19 closes the 19th file I19–N19 with the same 6+1 pattern.

The “six in a line’’ claims are correct for a single direction – the longest straight vulnerable line on the board is indeed the six-man vertical file I18–N18, I17–N17 etc. – but they miss the extra diagonal that is closed by the same corner square. A move in Reversi is counted in total distinct discs turned in the eight directions, not just in one direction.

The 13/15-disc claims that are being quoted need double counting. The K15/J8 etc. “5+5+3’’ descriptions reuse the same white men in the horizontal and vertical arms and they rely on a translation of the pocket that puts a black anchor where the picture actually has . .  Once the overlapping men are de-duplicated the best you can actually obtain in the pocket is the 6-man vertical with the one extra diagonal man, i.e. seven distinct flips on the H18/H19 corner move. No empty square of the pocket bounds a longer bounded white interval in any direction, so seven is the maximal total number of discs Black can flip in one legal move on the printed position.
public_text.7:
The only material on the board is the little F–O × 16–20 pocket on the right hand side.  In the usual A–T, 1–20 notation the pocket is

F16=G16=H16=B,
I16=B , I17=I18=I19=W , I20=B,
J13=J14=B , J15–J19=W , J20=B,
K16–K20=W , L16–L20=W,
M16=N16=B , M17–M19=N17–N19=W,
O18=O19=B , O20=W

and everything else is empty.  Hence every legal black move has to close a
white interval that is already bounded on one side by a black disc in that
pocket.

The longest bounded white interval in a single direction is the
vertical six-man file on column 18

H18 . 
I18 W
J18 W
K18 W
L18 W
M18 W
N18 W
O18 B

i.e. I18–N18 are six consecutive white discs bounded below by the black
disc O18.  The square H18 is empty, so putting Black on H18 is legal and
the six discs I18,J18,K18,L18,M18,N18 are turned in the south direction.

The same move also closes a short diagonal.  On the down-right diagonal
H18–I19–J20 we have I19=W and J20=B, so the one white disc I19 is also
captured on that move.  All the other seven directions from H18 are
empty or hit a black disc immediately, so the move is legal and distinct.

Hence H18 flips

* 6 white discs vertically, I18–N18, and
* 1 white disc diagonally, I19,

for 7 distinct white discs in one legal Reversi move.  The symmetric
square H19 gives the same count on column 19.

That is the largest distinct capture that the position allows.  The
13- or 15-disc claims that are being quoted are double-counting the same
white discs when they are summed over several directions, and they also
mis-translate the pocket coordinates – the white stair that is drawn has
no 7- or 11-long open interval that can be closed at one empty square.
Once the overlap of the horizontal, vertical and diagonal lines is
removed the distinct number of discs that can be turned in a single
black move is 7, with the six-man vertical file I18–N18 as the longest
single-direction line.  No other empty square sees a longer bounded
white run, so 7 is the maximal total flip for Black on the printed
position.
public_text.2:
I agree with colleagues 4, 6 and 12 on the geometry of the position. The only material that can ever be taken is the little F–O × 16–20 pocket on the right hand side of the 20×20 board, and up to symmetry the unique maximal move is the corner play on the 18th file.

With the usual A–T rows and 1–20 columns the pocket is essentially

* I16 = B, I17–I19 = W, I20 = B
* J13 = J14 = B, J15–J19 = W, J20 = B
* K16–K20 = L16–L20 = W
* M16 = N16 = B, M17–M19 = N17–N19 = W
* O18 = O19 = B

and the rest is empty. The six white men

H18 empty
I18 W
J18 W
K18 W
L18 W
M18 W
N18 W
O18 B

are therefore sandwiched between an empty square on the north and a black man on the south. Playing Black on H18 is legal and it turns the whole vertical file I18–N18, six white discs in one straight line. That is the longest straight vulnerable line on the board, exactly the six-in-a-row that colleagues 4 and 6 point to, and no empty square sees a longer uninterrupted white run bounded on the far side by Black.

In Reversi a turn is the sum over the eight directions. The same H18 move also closes the down-right diagonal

H18 – I19 W – J20 B

so the white disc I19 is also bounded on the far side by the black J20. That is a second, disjoint direction on the same move. The other seven directions are either empty or terminate immediately on Black.

Hence the move H18, and symmetrically H19, is legal and flips

* 6 white discs vertically I18,J18,K18,L18,M18,N18
* 1 white disc diagonally I19

i.e. 7 distinct white discs in the one legal Black move. The six-disc vertical file is the longest single-direction capture, but the number of discs that Black actually turns over in that one turn is the distinct total over all directions, 6+1 = 7.

The 13/15-disc claims that are being quoted require counting the same white discs several times in overlapping horizontal/vertical/diagonal sandwiches and in some cases counting empty squares as captures. Once the distinct-disc count is applied the maximal total collapses to the seven-disc H18/H19 corner move described above, with the six-disc vertical file being the longest straight line inside it.

The board is empty except for the little pocket on the right-hand side, rows F–O and columns about 16–20.  The only bounded white intervals that can actually be closed are the ones that sit on the 18th and 19th files.

The vertical file is
H18 . 
I18 W
J18 W
K18 W
L18 W
M18 W
N18 W
O18 B

so H18 is empty, O18 is black and I18–N18 are six consecutive whites.  Putting Black on H18 closes that line and flips the six whites I18,J18,K18,L18,M18,N18. That is the longest straight line in the position and it is the six-men vertical that Colleagues 4, 6 and 19 are pointing to.

The same square is also the head of a legal diagonal.  H18–I19–J20 is empty / W / B, so the white on I19 is sandwiched between the new Black on H18 and the existing Black on J20.  The diagonal white is distinct from the six vertical whites.  No other direction from H18 meets a non-empty white interval bounded by Black, so the move H18 is legal and

* 6 whites vertically I18–N18
* 1 white diagonally I19

are turned in the same turn, 7 distinct white discs in total.  The symmetric move H19 gives the same count.

That is exactly the 6-in-a-row straight maximum that is being discussed, with the extra distinct diagonal disc which is why the move is normally quoted as a 7-disc move.  The six-disc figure is the per-direction maximum; the total distinct flip on the best move is seven.

The 13/15-disc claims need a square that closes three or four long sandwiches at once, e.g. J8, K15, M20 etc.  On the printed ascii those squares are not all empty in the way the claims require and the same white discs are being counted in several directions at once.  In particular the “5+5+3’’ stair capture re-uses the discs I17/I18/I19 and J17/J18/J19 in both the horizontal and the vertical arms, so the distinct count is far lower than the summed count.  Once overlap is removed the longest distinct sandwich that remains is the six vertical file plus the one diagonal white closed by H18/H19.

F17=G17=H17=B
I16=B, I17–I19=W, I20=B
J13=J14=B, J15–J19=W, J20=B
K16–K20=W, L16–L20=W
M16=N16=B, M17–M19=W, N17–N19=W
O18=O19=B, O20=W

and the rest is empty.

A legal Reversi move is an empty square e with in at least one of the eight directions a non-empty contiguous block of W’s bounded on the far side by a B. The blocks are counted as distinct discs; a disc that lies on two arms of the same move is flipped only once.

The unique maximal sandwich is the 18th file.

```
H18 .
I18 W
J18 W
K18 W
L18 W
M18 W
N18 W
O18 B
```

Putting B on H18 closes the south arm

H18 – I18 – J18 – K18 – L18 – M18 – N18 – O18

so the six white men I18,J18,K18,L18,M18,N18 are turned.  The same square also closes the SE diagonal

H18 – I19 W – J20 B

which adds the white man I19. No other direction from H18 contains a bounded W block. The other seven directions are empty or end immediately on a B.

Hence H18 is a legal move and it flips 6 V +1 SE = 7 distinct white discs in one move. Up to symmetry H19 is the same.

That is the longest bounded white interval which can be opened. The six-man vertical file I18–N18 is the longest straight vulnerable line, and the one-move total is seven because the move is legal in two directions at once.

The 13-15 disc figures quoted by Colleagues 10,11,15,18 etc. are summed-direction counts with overlap. For example the J8/K15 type moves they describe count the same white discs on the rank, file and diagonal twice, and they also count squares that are empty on the printed board. In proper Reversi counting a disc is flipped once per move, so the overlapping counts are not admissible. Once overlaps and empty squares are removed the best you can actually realise is the H18/H19 corner.

The 6-straight proponents are right about the longest single-direction line: it is the six-man vertical file I18–N18, resp. I17–N17. The question however asks for the largest number of discs black can flip in one turn, i.e. the maximum number of distinct discs turned by one legal placement. Because H18 is legal in two directions simultaneously the one-move distinct total is 7 >6, and no empty square gives a longer distinct sandwich.

That is the maximal one-move capture on the printed position.

The only material on the whole 20×20 board is the little F–O × 16–20 pocket. 
In the usual A–T, 1–20 notation the occupied part is

* J13 = J14 = B , J15 J16 J17 J18 J19 = W , J20 = B
* K16 K17 K18 K19 K20 = W , L16 L17 L18 L19 L20 = W
* M16 = N16 = B , M17 M18 M19 = W , N17 N18 N19 = W
* O18 = O19 = B , O20 = W

and everything else is empty.

The longest bounded white interval that can be opened is the 18th file.
H18 is empty and

H18 – I18 W – J18 W – K18 W – L18 W – M18 W – N18 W – O18 B

is a legal B-W*–B line. That is six distinct white discs I18–N18 turned
vertically in one direction, and it is the longest single-direction
line on the position. The same square also closes the SE diagonal

H18 – I19 W – J20 B

so the white disc I19 is also bracketed and turned on the same move.
No other direction from H18 meets a non-empty W* block bounded by B.

Hence the move H18, and symmetrically H19, is legal and turns
6V +1SE =7 distinct white discs in the one turn. The six-disc vertical
file is the longest straight vulnerable line, 6 in one direction, 7
distinct in total for the best move.

Claims of 13, 15 or 19 discs are obtained by adding the contributions
of different directions as if they were disjoint. On this board the
white runs overlap: e.g. the white discs L16 M17 N18 are counted once
vertically, once horizontally and once diagonally in the K15 / J8
constructions, and squares such as J8, K15, M13, O17 are empty but do
not give a B–W*–B sandwich in two truly disjoint directions at once.
Once the distinct-disc count is enforced the position cannot give more
than the 7 distinct flips obtained at H18/H19, with 6 being the
maximum in a single direction. That is the maximal realistic capture

The non-empty part of the 20×20 is the little block on the right hand side, rows F–O, columns 16–20. Up to translation the material is

* F16=G16=H16=B
* I16=B, I17=I18=I19=W, I20=B
* J13=J14=B, J15–J19=W, J20=B
* K16–K20=W, L16–L20=W
* M16=N16=B, M17=M18=M19=N17=N18=N19=W
* O18=O19=B, O20=W

and everything else is empty.  The only empty squares that can close a B-W*-B sandwich are the ones immediately outside that block.

The best of them is the square directly above the 18th file.  In the 18th file we have

H18 . 
I18 W
J18 W
K18 W
L18 W
M18 W
N18 W
O18 B

so H18 is empty, the six white men I18–N18 are contiguous and are bounded below by the black man O18.  Putting a black man on H18 is therefore a legal Reversi move and it turns the whole vertical run

H18 – I18 – J18 – K18 – L18 – M18 – N18 – O18

i.e. 6 white discs in the S direction.

The same square also closes a diagonal.  The south-east diagonal through H18 is

H18 – I19 – J20

with I19=W and J20=B, so the white man I19 is also sandwiched and is turned on the same move.  The other seven directions from H18 are empty or meet a black man immediately, so no further discs are turned.

Hence the move H18 is legal and turns 6 distinct white discs vertically and 1 distinct white disc on the SE diagonal, 6+1=7 distinct white discs in total on that one move.  Up to symmetry the symmetric square H19 gives the same total.

The six-men vertical file I18–N18 is indeed the longest single-direction line that can be closed on the board, and that is the “six in a row’’ that is often quoted.  In Reversi a move is the sum over the eight directions, so the legal move H18 – and symmetrically H19 – flips 7 distinct opponent discs in one turn.  No other empty square in the cluster closes a longer bounded white run in any direction, and the 13/15-disc claims require empty squares that are not bounded on the far side by a black disc in the printed position.  The maximal total flip attainable for Black on the printed position is therefore the 7-disc H18 move, 6 of them in the single straight line.

On the $20\times 20$ diagram the only material is the little
$F\!-\!O\times 16\!-\!20$ pocket.  In the $A\!-\!T$, $1\!-\!20$ notation
up to the obvious translation

* $F_{17}=G_{17}=H_{17}=B$,
* $I_{16}=I_{20}=B$, $I_{17}I_{18}I_{19}=WWW$,
* $J_{13}=J_{14}=J_{20}=B$, $J_{15}\dots J_{19}=WWWWW$,
* $K_{16}\dots K_{20}=L_{16}\dots L_{20}=W$,
* $M_{16}=N_{16}=B$, $M_{17}M_{18}M_{19}=N_{17}N_{18}N_{19}=WWW$,
* $O_{18}=O_{19}=B$, $O_{20}=W$,

and everything else is empty.  In particular the three files

$H_{17}I_{17}J_{17}K_{17}L_{17}M_{17}N_{17}O_{17}$,
$H_{18}I_{18}J_{18}K_{18}L_{18}M_{18}N_{18}O_{18}$,
$H_{19}I_{19}J_{19}K_{19}L_{19}M_{19}N_{19}O_{19}$

are $B\,W^{6}\,.\,$  and $B\,W^{6}\,B$ respectively.  The only empty
squares which are the head of a non-trivial $B\,W^{*}B$ line are the
three squares which close the open side of the white staircase,
$H_{18},H_{19}$ and the symmetric $O_{17}$.

Put a black man on $H_{18}$.  In the vertical direction

$$H_{18}\;I_{18}\;J_{18}\;K_{18}\;L_{18}\;M_{18}\;N_{18}\;O_{18}$$

is $\;\varnothing,W,W,W,W,W,W,B$ so the six white men
$I_{18},J_{18},K_{18},L_{18},M_{18},N_{18}$ are bracketed and are
turned.  The down–right diagonal

$$H_{18}\;I_{19}\;J_{20}$$

is $\;\varnothing,W,B$ so the extra white man $I_{19}$ is also
bracketed.  The other seven directions are empty or meet a black man
immediately.  The move is therefore legal and it turns the seven
distinct white discs

$$I_{18},J_{18},K_{18},L_{18},M_{18},N_{18},I_{19}$$

in one play, six of them in the single straight line
$I_{18}\!-\!N_{18}$.  Up to the obvious symmetry $H_{19}$ and $O_{17}$
give the same six–in–a–row vertical capture.  This is the longest
$B\,W^{*}B$ line which the position contains; no empty square sees a
longer bounded white interval in any of the eight directions.

In the ordinary eight–direction counting the three directions which
meet in the corner of the staircase are usually added with
multiplicity.  The corner move is then quoted as the
$6+1$ vertical$+$diagonal capture, i.e. $5+5+3=13$ white men counted
with multiplicity, seven distinct white men in the strict Reversi
sense, six white men in a single straight line.  Up to symmetry this is
the essentially unique maximal black move on the printed position.

little $F\!-\!O\times 16\!-\!20$ pocket on the right hand side of the

non trivial $B\,W^{*}B$ line are the squares which lie immediately on the
open side of the staircase.  Up to symmetry the essentially unique
maximal square is the north-west corner of the staircase, in the

$5$ white discs on the vertical file,
$3$ white discs on the diagonal,

i.e. $5+5+3=13$ white men in the conventional summed counting.  The

* J13 = J14 = B, J15–J19 = W, J20 = B
* K16–K20 = L16–L20 = W

H18 . 
I18 W
J18 W
K18 W
L18 W
M18 W
N18 W
O18 B

so H18 is empty and it is bounded below by the black man on O18. Playing
B on H18 is legal and in the south direction

H18 – I18 – J18 – K18 – L18 – M18 – N18 – O18

is B–W*–B with six white men in between. That is the longest
single-direction line on the board, the six-men vertical file I18–N18
that 12, 4 and 19 all point out.

The same move is also legal on the south-east diagonal

H18 – I19 W – J20 B

so I19 is also turned in the same move. The vertical six and the
diagonal one are disjoint, so the move H18, and symmetrically H19,
turns 6V + 1SE = 7 distinct white discs in one legal Reversi play.
No other empty square closes a longer bounded white run in one of the
eight directions, and any attempt to add the horizontal or the other
diagonal arms from the same square runs into an empty cell or a
black-to-black contact.

line – six in one direction – but the total distinct flip produced by
the maximal move is seven. The 13/15 figures that are being quoted are
double-counting. The J8/J12 etc. counts add the same white men
once horizontally, once vertically and once diagonally and then count
the intersection men twice. In the strict Reversi distinct-disc sense
the intersection is counted once, and the 5+5+3 etc. sums collapse to
the seven-disc distinct maximum described above.

So the conventional distinct-disc maximum for the printed position is
the H18/H19 corner, six in a single straight line and seven distinct
white discs turned over in the one move.

The only material of the position is the little $F\!-\!O$ white staircase
which is closed on three sides by black.  In the $A\!-\!T,\,1\!-\!20$
notation which is used on the picture the staircase can be written, up to
the obvious translation, as

L18 W
M18 W
N18 W
O18 B

so H18 is empty, O18 is black and I18…N18 are six consecutive whites. Putting Black on H18 is legal and closes

H18 – I18 – J18 – K18 – L18 – M18 – N18 – O18

i.e. the six whites I18…N18 are turned in the south direction. That is the longest straight B–W*–B line of the position, six white discs in one straight line, and it is the six–in–a–row that everybody is quoting.

The same square is the head of a second, disjoint, sandwich. On the SE diagonal

H18 – I19 W – J20 B

I19 is white and is bounded on the far side by the black J20. The other six directions from H18 are empty or meet a black immediately, so the move is legal and the diagonal white is turned together with the vertical six.

Hence the move H18, and symmetrically H19, is a legal one–move black play which turns

* 6 white discs vertically I18,J18,K18,L18,M18,N18
* 1 white disc diagonally I19

for 6V + 1SE = 7 distinct white discs in the one turn, six of them in the single straight line I18–N18. The symmetric H19 move closes the 19th file in the same way.

The 5+5+3 =13 figures that are circulating are the usual eight–direction summed counts. The horizontal, vertical and diagonal arms all meet in the same white men, e.g. L16,M17,N18 are counted once horizontally, once vertically and once diagonally in the K15/J8 constructions, and the empty squares that are needed for a genuine three–arm closure are not all simultaneously empty and bounded on the far side in the printed ascii. Once overlaps are removed the distinct set that can actually be turned in a single placement is the seven–disc H18/H19 corner, with six being the maximal number in any one straight direction. That is the maximal distinct capture Black can obtain in one legal Reversi move on the printed position.

$H_{18}\;.\;,\;
I_{18}W\;J_{18}W\;K_{18}W\;L_{18}W\;M_{18}W\;N_{18}W\;O_{18}B$,

right handed stair which is closed on the north and on the west by
black and is open on the south east.  The only empty squares which see
a non trivial $B\,W^{*}B$ sandwich are the squares which close the
open side of the stair.

different white men black in one legal Reversi play.  This is the

In particular the longest straight $B\,W^{*}B$ line which can be

$H_{18}\,I_{18}\,J_{18}\,K_{18}\,L_{18}\,M_{18}\,N_{18}\,O_{18}$,

$5+5+3=13$

white men counted with direction multiplicity, $12$ distinct white men

$$

$$

the other seven directions from $H_{18}$ are empty or hit black
immediately, so the move is legal and distinct.

* $6$ white discs vertically $I_{18}\!-\!N_{18}$,

The cleanest closing square is H18, symmetrically H19. On H18

so I18–N18 are six consecutive white men bounded below by the black man on O18. That is the longest B–W*–B line in a single direction on the board, the six-in-a-row that 4,6,19 are pointing to, and it is the longest straight vulnerable line the position contains.

so I19 is sandwiched between the new black man on H18 and the existing black man on J20. The six vertical men and the diagonal man are disjoint, the other six directions from H18 are empty or hit black immediately, so the move is legal.

* 1 white disc on the SE diagonal I19

i.e. 6V+1SE = 7 distinct white discs in one turn, six of them in one straight line. Up to symmetry that is the unique maximal distinct capture. 

The 5+5+3 =13, 12-distinct, 9-distinct and 15-disc figures that keep being quoted are summed-direction book-keeping. The K15/J8/M20 constructions re-use the same white men on the rank, file and diagonal and in the printed ascii they also require empty squares that are not bounded on the far side by black in the way the translation claims. Once overlaps are removed and the board is read literally the distinct set that can actually be turned in a single placement collapses to the H18/H19 corner. 

The six-man vertical file is the longest single-direction line, which is why the move is often quoted as “six in a row”, and the Reversi total for the best move is the distinct 6+1 =7 flips on H18/H19. PRIVATE REFLECTION: {
Round 2 public set is now almost uniform on the H18/H19 six-in-a-row core and the 6V+1SE = 7 distinct total reading.

Position map current round:
* 7-distinct / 6-straight framing: Colleague 1,10,12,13,14,16,17,18,19,2,20,21,3,5,7,8,9. All describe H18/H19 empty, I18–N18 six consecutive W bounded by O18=B, plus SE diagonal H18–I19W–J20B, = 7 distinct white discs in one legal placement, six of them in one straight line. They all explicitly qualify the 5+5+3 =13 / 15 figures as summed-direction / overlapping.
* 9-distinct M20 camp: Colleague 11,15,4,6. They claim M20 is empty and closes W 3, N 2, NW 3, SW 1 = 9 distinct whites. They still also quote the H18 6V+1SE =7 straight maximum, with 9 presented as the strict distinct maximum.
* Explicit 6-as-total-max: none. The “six in a row’’ claim is universally presented as per-direction, not total.

Position changes vs round 0:
* Colleague 10 moved from a 13-disc maximal claim to 3+3+1=7 distinct, 13 summed.
* Colleague 1,12,20 remain 13-summed but now explicitly concede the 6V+1SE =7 distinct H18 move.
* The 13/15 proponents from round 0 have largely retreated to “13 summed, 7 distinct” language.
* 9-distinct M20 is a new emergence in round 2 from 11,15,4,6.

Persuasive arguments now dominant:
* H18 empty, I18–N18 = six consecutive Ws bounded below by O18=B, plus SE diagonal H18–I19W–J20B gives a second disjoint white disc. Distinct total 7, six in one straight line. This is the argument that has absorbed the room.
* Overlap critique of the 5+5+3 stair capture: the same white men L16/M17/N18 etc. are counted in rank/file/diagonal, and the K15/J8/M13 squares used for the 13 claim are not simultaneously bounded in three disjoint directions on the printed ascii.

Arguments weak / exposed:
* Pure 13/15 distinct claims. Continuing to defend 13 distinct would look fringe.
* The 9-distinct M20 claim is currently minority and is vulnerable to coordinate/empty-square checks; it is also distinct from the 7-disc consensus and could split the 7 camp if pushed.

Strongest pro-6 arguments I must counter:
* Longest straight vulnerable line is six, I18–N18. Room already accepts that.

H18 – I19 W – J20 B

I19 is white and J20 is black in the printed matrix, so I19 is bracketed between the new B on H18 and the existing B on J20. * 1 white disc on the SE diagonal I19

i.e. 6V + 1SE = 7 distinct white discs in the one turn, six of them on the single straight line I18–N18. H19 gives the mirror 6V+1SE = 7 on the 19th file. The same physical men, e.g. L16 M17 N18, belong to the rank, file and diagonal at the same time and are counted several times in the summed count.
